definition_zh: 非常；很；（限定用法）正是那个；极端的
definition_en: to a high degree, and, before a noun, the actual or exact one
core_image: 温度计的红柱一路顶到最上面那格
scene: 面试官看完简历，抬头说了一句：这份作品集非常出色。The interviewer said that the portfolio was very impressive.
sceneCN: 这里 very 是「非常」（第 1 个义项：表示程度很高）；句意为面试官说这份作品集非常出色。温度计顶格的那个画面就是这个副词给人的感觉。

derivatives.zh: 短语，义为「非常；十分」
古旧副词，义为「确实地；真正地」

senses.title: To a high degree
senses.definition: used to strengthen an adjective or another adverb
senses.definitionCN: 用来加强形容词或副词的程度
senses.example: The interviewer said the portfolio was very impressive.
senses.exampleCN: 面试官说这份作品集非常出色。
senses.why: The oldest job of the word is simply to push a quality higher.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的作用，就是把某种性质往上推高。

senses.title: In a high degree with verbs
senses.definition: used with some verbs and participles to mean greatly
senses.definitionCN: 与某些动词或分词连用，表示程度很高
senses.example: She was very pleased with the result.
senses.exampleCN: 她对结果非常满意。
senses.why: With a participle the same word shifts from modifying a quality to modifying an action.
senses.whyCN: 与分词连用时，同一个词从修饰性质转为修饰动作。

senses.title: The actual or exact one
senses.definition: used before a noun to single out the exact person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，指出正是某个人或某个事物
senses.example: That is the very book I was looking for.
senses.exampleCN: 那正是我在找的那本书。
senses.why: Pointing at one exact item is a short step from pushing a quality to its limit.
senses.whyCN: 从把性质推向极限，到指出唯一确切的那一个，只是一小步。

senses.title: The extreme end of something
senses.definition: used with a noun to mean the extreme or utmost
senses.definitionCN: 与名词连用，表示极端或极致
senses.example: They searched to the very end of the cave.
senses.exampleCN: 他们一直搜到洞穴的最深处。
senses.why: If a quality is pushed to the top, the noun that carries it is at its extreme.
senses.whyCN: 性质既被推到顶端，承载它的名词也就处在极端处。

senses.title: Used to add force in speech
senses.definition: used in speech for emphasis, as in the very idea
senses.definitionCN: 用于口语中加强语气，如 the very idea
senses.example: The very idea of moving abroad frightened him.
senses.exampleCN: 一想到要搬到国外，他就害怕。
senses.why: Emphasis in speech takes the same intensifying force and turns it on an idea.
senses.whyCN: 口语里的强调，把这股加强的力量转而用在某个念头上。

intro.en: Very began as a French adjective meaning true, and turned into the intensifier we use today.
intro.cn: very 最初是法语中意为「真实的」的形容词，后来变成今天的程度副词。

items.en: Verus meant true, and verax named the one who tells the truth.
items.cn: verus 意为真实的，verax 指说真话的人。

items.en: French verai carried the sense of genuine into everyday speech.
items.cn: 法语 verai 把「真正的」这一含义带入日常口语。

items.en: English verray first meant true or real, as in a verray friend.
items.cn: 中世纪英语 verray 最初意为真实的，如 a verray friend（真正的朋友）。

items.en: Placed before an adjective, it began to mean in a true degree, hence greatly.
items.cn: 放在形容词前时，它开始表示「真正地…」，进而表示「非常」。

items.en: The old sense survives only in fixed phrases such as the very same.
items.cn: 旧义如今只保留在 the very same 这类固定短语中。

note.en: The first group holds the small family of forms, the second the intensifiers and their opposites.
note.cn: 第一组是同族的小词群，第二组是程度副词及其反义说法。

entries.definition: to check that something is true

normalIntro.en: From a Latin word for true to a word that simply turns the volume up: very has kept only its force.
normalIntro.cn: 从拉丁语中表示「真实」的词，到只负责把音量调大的词：very 只留下了那股加强的力量。

normal.en: Very and verify share the Latin root verus, true.
normal.cn: very 与 verify 同出拉丁语 verus（真实的）。

normal.en: Before a noun it means exact: the very man.
normal.cn: 放在名词前表示确切：the very man（正是那个人）。

normal.en: Before an adjective it means greatly: very cold.
normal.cn: 放在形容词前表示程度高：very cold（很冷）。

normal.en: It does not modify verbs directly; say very much like, not very like.
normal.cn: 它不直接修饰动词；要说 very much like，而非 very like。

normal.en: Comparative forms verier and veriest survive only in old books.
normal.cn: 比较级 verier、最高级 veriest 只存在于旧书中。

abstract.en: Picture a thermometer whose red line goes to the top mark.
abstract.cn: 想一支温度计的红线顶到最上面一格。

abstract.en: Feel a speaker leaning forward to press one word harder.
abstract.cn: 感受说话人身子前倾，把某一个词压得更重。

abstract.en: See a spotlight picking out one single chair on a stage.
abstract.cn: 想聚光灯在舞台上圈出唯一一把椅子。

examples.en: The soup is very hot, so let it cool for a minute.
examples.cn: 汤很烫，让它凉一分钟。

examples.en: This is the very place where the two roads meet.
examples.cn: 这里正是两条路交汇的地方。

examples.en: He was not very happy about the change of plan.
examples.cn: 他对计划的变更不太满意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「外瑞」——外边那位瑞哥嗓门特别大，一说就是「非常」响。

root: 拉丁语 verus（真实的）→ 古法语 verai → 中世纪英语 verray（真正的）→ 现代英语 very（非常）

sensesIntro.en: One little word grows from true, through truly to a plain intensifier, and keeps a second life as exactly that one.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个小词从「真实」出发，经「真正地」变成纯粹的程度副词，又保留了「正是那一个」的第二重身份。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thermometer pushed to its top mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：温度计被推到最高那一格。

branches.en: The degree branch: a portfolio called impressive.
branches.cn: 程度分支：被称作出色的作品集。

branches.en: The verb branch: very pleased with the result.
branches.cn: 动词分支：对结果非常满意。

branches.en: The pointing branch: the very book on the shelf.
branches.cn: 指认分支：架上正是那本书。

branches.en: The extreme branch: the very end of the cave.
branches.cn: 极端分支：洞穴的最深处。

branches.en: The emphasis branch: the very idea frightens him.
branches.cn: 强调分支：光是这个念头就让他害怕。

intro.en: There is no living prefix here; the old root ver- (true) survives mainly inside longer words.
intro.cn: 这个词没有可拆的活前缀，古词根 ver-（真实）主要存活在更长的词里。

latinIntro.en: Latin verus gave French verai and English very; the same root also built verify, verity, and verdict.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 verus 派生法语 verai 与英语 very，同一词根还构成 verify、verity、verdict。

items.example: Ver- hides inside very as the sense of the genuine.
items.exampleCN: ver- 藏在 very 里，是「真正」的含义。

items.example: Very first meant in a true way.
items.exampleCN: very 最初表示「以真实的方式」。

items.example: We verify the figures before printing.
items.exampleCN: 付印前我们会核实这些数字。

items.meaning: a true saying by a jury
items.example: The jury returned a verdict of not guilty.
The verity of the claim was never in doubt.
items.exampleCN: 这一说法的真实性从未被怀疑。

items.example: She enjoyed the trip very much.
They wore the very same coat.
items.exampleCN: 他们穿的是完全相同的外套。

items.example: The film was not very long.
Utterly is stronger than very.

definition_zh: 老兵；退伍军人；老手；（美）经验丰富的人
definition_en: a person who has served in the armed forces, or who has long experience in a field
core_image: 一位老兵胸前挂满勋章站在队列最前面
scene: 纪念日游行上，一位老兵被请到最前面，人群为他鼓掌。A veteran of the war led the parade with a slow, steady step.
sceneCN: 这里 veteran 是「老兵」（第 1 个义项：在军队中服役过的人）；句意为一位老兵迈着缓慢而稳的步子领着游行队伍。胸前挂满勋章的那个人就是这个词的形象。

collocations.zh: 经历过两次战争的老兵

derivatives.zh: 由 veteran 加 -ship 构成，义为「老兵身份；老练」
同源词，来自 veterinarius（管牲口的人），义为「兽医的」
加前缀 in- 构成，义为「积习难改的；根深蒂固的」

senses.title: A soldier who has served for long
senses.definition: someone who has served a long time in the armed forces
senses.definitionCN: 在军队中长期服役或曾经服役的人
senses.example: A veteran of the war led the parade with a slow, steady step.
senses.exampleCN: 一位战争老兵迈着缓慢而稳的步子领着游行队伍。
senses.why: Latin veteranus was the word for an old soldier, and that is still the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 veteranus 本来就是「老士兵」，这至今仍是首要义项。

senses.title: Someone with deep experience
senses.definition: a person who has a lot of experience in a job or activity
senses.definitionCN: 在工作或活动中经验丰富的人
senses.example: She is a veteran of three national campaigns.
senses.exampleCN: 她是三次全国性竞选的老手。
senses.why: Old soldiers were valued for their years in the field, and the same word was lent to other fields.
senses.whyCN: 老兵的可靠来自多年的战场经验，这个词随后被借到别的领域。

senses.title: A vehicle or article long in use
senses.definition: a thing that has been used a long time and done good service
senses.definitionCN: 使用多年、立过功的旧车或旧物
senses.example: He still drives his veteran car on weekends.
senses.exampleCN: 周末他仍开着自己那辆老牌车。
senses.why: The idea of long service applies to machines as to people.
senses.whyCN: 「服役多年」的想法既可以用于人，也可以用于机器。

senses.title: The adjective for long-tested skill
senses.definition: having long experience and therefore being reliable
senses.definitionCN: 有长久经验因而可靠的
senses.example: A veteran teacher knows which question to ask first.
senses.exampleCN: 经验丰富的老师知道先问哪个问题。
senses.why: Once a noun of experience, the word can sit before another noun as a badge of reliability.
senses.whyCN: 这个词一旦表示经验，就可以放在别的名词前，作为可靠的标记。

senses.title: A former serviceman recognised by the state
senses.definition: a former member of the forces entitled to state support
senses.definitionCN: 依法享有国家优待的退役军人
senses.example: The clinic offers free care for veterans.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所为退伍军人提供免费治疗。
senses.why: Once service ends, the word turns into an official label with rights attached.
senses.whyCN: 服役结束之后，这个词又变成附带权利的官方身份。

intro.en: Veteran came straight from Latin veteranus, an old soldier, from vetus, old.
intro.cn: veteran 直接来自拉丁语 veteranus（老士兵），源于 vetus（老的）。

items.en: Vetus meant old, and veteranus named an old soldier.
items.cn: vetus 意为老的，veteranus 指老士兵。

items.en: Roman writers also used vetera for things long in use.
items.cn: 罗马作家也用 vetera 指使用很久的东西。

items.en: English adopted veteran in the sixteenth century for long-serving soldiers.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪引入 veteran，指服役已久的军人。

items.en: Through the nineteenth century it spread to any long-tested worker.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，它扩展到任何久经考验的从业者。

items.en: The adjective uses now include veteran services and veteran cars.
items.cn: 如今形容词用法包括退伍军人服务和老牌老爷车。

note.en: The first group holds words built on the same stem, the second the close words for an experienced person.
note.cn: 第一组是同词干的词，第二组是表示有经验者的相近词。

entries.definition: long established and hard to change
an old car kept in good order

normalIntro.en: Latin vetus, old, is the whole secret: a veteran is simply someone who has been around a long time.
normalIntro.cn: 全部秘密就在拉丁语 vetus（老的）：veteran 就是待得够久的人。

normal.en: Veteran, veterinary, and inveterate all rest on Latin vetus, old.
normal.cn: veteran、veterinary、inveterate 都建立在拉丁语 vetus（老的）之上。

normal.en: Picture the oldest head in the line, wearing the most medals.
normal.cn: 想队列中最年长的那颗头，挂的勋章最多。

normal.en: The word moved from soldiers to any long-serving worker.
normal.cn: 这个词从士兵扩展到任何长期从业的人。

normal.en: The plural is plain veterans, no doubling.
normal.cn: 复数是直接的 veterans，不双写辅音。

normal.en: Before another noun it becomes an adjective: veteran teacher.
normal.cn: 放在另一个名词前就作形容词：veteran teacher。

abstract.en: See one slow, steady step leading a whole parade.
abstract.cn: 想一个缓慢而稳的步子带着整支队伍前进。

abstract.en: Think of an old coat that has lasted through many winters.
abstract.cn: 想一件熬过许多个冬天的旧大衣。

abstract.en: Hear medals click softly against each other as he walks.
abstract.cn: 听勋章随着脚步轻轻相碰。

examples.en: My grandfather is a veteran who served for twenty years.
examples.cn: 我祖父是一位服役二十年的老兵。

examples.en: She is a veteran of the newspaper world.
examples.cn: 她是报界的老手。

examples.en: Veteran staff were asked to train the newcomers.
examples.cn: 资深员工被安排去培训新人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「维特伦」——老魏特守在队伍最前面，是个老兵。

root: 拉丁语 vetus（老的）→ veteranus（老士兵）→ 法语 vétéran → 英语 veteran

sensesIntro.en: A Latin word for old grows from long service in the army, to skill in any trade, to old machines and official standing.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个拉丁语中表示「老」的词，从军队里的长期服役，长到各行各业的熟练，再长到旧机器与官方身份。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old soldier leading a parade.
core.cn: 核心意象：一位老兵领着游行队伍。

branches.en: The army branch: a soldier of the old war.
branches.cn: 军队分支：上一场战争的老兵。

branches.en: The career branch: veteran of three campaigns.
branches.cn: 职业分支：三次竞选的老手。

branches.en: The machine branch: the old car driven on Sundays.
branches.cn: 机器分支：周末才开的老牌车。

branches.en: The adjective branch: the veteran teacher who knows what to ask.
branches.cn: 形容词分支：知道先问什么的资深教师。

branches.en: The rights branch: free care for veterans.
branches.cn: 权利分支：为退伍军人提供免费医疗。

intro.en: The stem veter- carries old, and endings such as -an and -ship build the family.
intro.cn: 词干 veter- 携带「老」的含义，-an、-ship 等后缀构成这个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin vetus gave veteranus, and English also borrowed veterinarian and the prefix in- form inveterate from the same stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vetus 派生 veteranus，英语还从同一词干借来 veterinarian 与带前缀的 inveterate。

items.example: Veter- holds the sense of long use.
items.exampleCN: veter- 携带「经久使用」之义。

items.example: A veteran was a person grown old in war.
items.exampleCN: veteran 原指在战争中变老的人。

items.example: Veteranship names the standing of a veteran.
Veterinary medicine deals with old and sick animals.
items.exampleCN: veterinary 医学处理的是老龄与生病的动物。

items.example: Inveterate means settled in by age.
items.exampleCN: inveterate 意为因年久而固定下来。

items.example: Recruits arrive while veterans stand guard.
items.exampleCN: 新兵到来时老兵在站岗。

items.example: A novice learns what a veteran knows.
items.exampleCN: 新手正在学习老兵已懂的东西。

items.example: An expert and a veteran are often the same person.
Veterans Day is marked in November.

definition_zh: 振动；震颤；（声音）回荡；颤动
definition_en: to move quickly and slightly to and fro, or to sound with a shaking tone
core_image: 手机静音放在桌面，屏幕亮起前桌子轻轻嗡了一下
scene: 车到站时，地板先轻微一颤，行李箱的拉杆跟着抖。The floor vibrated as the train pulled into the station.
sceneCN: 这里 vibrate 是「振动」（第 1 个义项：快速而轻微地来回运动）；句意为列车进站时地板在振动。桌上手机嗡一下的那种轻颤就是这个动作的意思。

derivatives.zh: 加后缀 -ion 构成，义为「振动；颤动」
现在分词作形容词，义为「震动的；颤动的」
加后缀 -atory 构成，义为「振动的」

senses.title: To shake quickly and slightly
senses.definition: to move back and forth very fast and with a small range
senses.definitionCN: 以很小的幅度快速来回运动
senses.example: The floor vibrated as the train pulled into the station.
senses.exampleCN: 列车进站时地板在震动。
senses.why: Latin vibrare described a swift, small shake, and that is still the core motion.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vibrare 指的正是快速而小幅的抖动，这仍是核心动作。

senses.title: To sound with a shaking tone
senses.definition: to produce or carry a sound that keeps shaking in the air
senses.definitionCN: 发出或在空气中持续震荡的声音
senses.example: His voice vibrated with anger.
senses.exampleCN: 他的声音因愤怒而发颤。
senses.why: A struck string shakes the air, and the shaking is what we hear as a living tone.
senses.whyCN: 被拨动的弦使空气震动，我们听到的那种「活」的音色就是这种震动。

senses.title: To be full of a strong feeling
senses.definition: to seem to shake with excitement, energy, or emotion
senses.definitionCN: 因兴奋、活力或情绪而显得震动
senses.example: The hall vibrated with applause.
senses.exampleCN: 大厅里掌声雷动。
senses.why: When a crowded room shakes with sound, the place itself seems to tremble.
senses.whyCN: 满场的声音让整个空间都在震，地方本身也仿佛在颤。

senses.title: Of a machine, to work with a hum
senses.definition: to run with a steady small shaking, as an engine does
senses.definitionCN: 如发动机那样带着持续的小幅震动运转
senses.example: The old fridge vibrates all night.
senses.exampleCN: 那台旧冰箱整夜嗡嗡作响。
senses.why: Machines turned the natural shake of matter into a daily background noise.
senses.whyCN: 机器把物质固有的抖动变成了日常的背景噪音。

senses.title: To swing between two choices
senses.definition: to move quickly between two states, as a mind between choices
senses.definitionCN: 像心思在两种选择间快速来回
senses.example: He vibrated between hope and fear.
senses.exampleCN: 他在希望与恐惧之间摇摆。
senses.why: A movement to and fro can describe a mind as easily as a string.
senses.whyCN: 来回摆动既可以形容琴弦，也可以形容心思。

intro.en: Vibrate comes from Latin vibrare, to shake or brandish, a motion small and fast.
intro.cn: vibrate 来自拉丁语 vibrare（抖动、挥舞），指的是一种小而快的运动。

items.en: Vibrare meant to shake, to quiver, and also to wave a weapon.
items.cn: vibrare 意为抖动、颤动，也表示挥舞武器。

items.en: The noun vibratio described a quivering movement.
items.cn: 名词 vibratio 描述颤动的运动。

items.en: English took vibrate in the seventeenth century, first for shaking bodies.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪引入 vibrate，最初用于物体的抖动。

items.en: Sound and engines gave the word its everyday modern senses.
items.cn: 声音与发动机赋予它现代日常的含义。

items.en: Phones added the sense of a silent buzz in the pocket.
items.cn: 手机又添上口袋里无声的一阵嗡动。

note.en: The first group holds the vibration family, the second the nearby verbs of shaking and steadying.
note.cn: 第一组是 vibration 词族，第二组是表示晃动与稳定的相近动词。

entries.definition: a shaking in a sung note
to move with larger, rougher force
to shake from fear or cold
to shake in a light, quick way

normalIntro.en: A slip of -ate on the Latin stem vibr- gives a verb for any fast, small shake.
normalIntro.cn: 在拉丁词干 vibr- 上加 -ate，就得到表示任何快速小抖动的动词。

normal.en: Vibrate, vibration, vibrant all share the Latin stem vibr-.
normal.cn: vibrate、vibration、vibrant 共有拉丁词干 vibr-。

normal.en: A string, a floor, a phone: the smaller the shake, the better the word.
normal.cn: 琴弦、地板、手机：抖得越小，越适合这个词。

normal.en: British stress falls on the second syllable, American often on the first.
normal.cn: 英式重音在第二音节，美式常在第一音节。

normal.en: Keep the final -e before -ion: vibration.
normal.cn: 加 -ion 前保留词尾 -e：vibration。

normal.en: Old Latin vibrare also meant to brandish a spear.
normal.cn: 古拉丁语 vibrare 还表示挥舞长矛。

abstract.en: Feel a phoned handset humming on a wooden table.
abstract.cn: 感受桌上的手机在震。

abstract.en: See a violin string after the bow has left it.
abstract.cn: 想琴弓离开后仍在颤的琴弦。

abstract.en: Hear a whole hall shaking with clapping.
abstract.cn: 听整个大厅被掌声震得发响。

examples.en: The windows vibrated whenever a truck went past.
examples.cn: 每当有卡车经过，窗户就震动。

examples.en: Her voice vibrated with excitement on the phone.
examples.cn: 电话里她的声音因兴奋而发颤。

examples.en: Set the phone to vibrate during the meeting.
examples.cn: 开会时把手机调成振动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「歪不瑞特」——歪着的架子不稳，一碰就抖个不停。

root: 拉丁语 vibrare（抖动；挥舞）→ vibratio（颤动）→ 英语 vibrate

sensesIntro.en: One verb of tiny fast motion grows into sound, into a crowded hall, into engines, and finally into a wavering mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个表示极快小幅运动的动词，长成声音、长成满场掌声、长成机器嗡鸣，最后长成摇摆不定的心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a phone buzzing on a wooden table.
core.cn: 核心意象：木桌上嗡动的手机。

branches.en: The motion branch: a floor shaking as the train arrives.
branches.cn: 运动分支：列车进站时震动的车厢地板。

branches.en: The sound branch: a voice shaking with anger.
branches.cn: 声音分支：因愤怒而颤抖的声音。

branches.en: The crowd branch: a hall trembling with applause.
branches.cn: 人群分支：被掌声震动的大厅。

branches.en: The machine branch: the fridge humming all night.
branches.cn: 机器分支：整夜嗡鸣的冰箱。

branches.en: The mind branch: swinging between hope and fear.
branches.cn: 心思分支：在希望与恐惧间摇摆。

intro.en: The Latin stem vibr- means to shake; -ate, -ion, and -ant build verb and nouns from it.
intro.cn: 拉丁词干 vibr- 意为抖动，-ate、-ion、-ant 由它构成动词与名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vibrare yielded English vibrate, vibration, and vibrant, all keeping the small quick shake.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vibrare 派生英语 vibrate、vibration、vibrant，都保留了小而快的抖动。

items.example: Vibr- carries the quivering motion.
Vibrate is the act of shaking.
Vibration names the shaking itself.
Vibrant means alive with quick energy.
items.exampleCN: vibrant 意为充满轻快活力的。

items.example: Vibratory motion is shaking motion.

items.meaning: to shake from fear or cold
items.example: He trembled, but the bridge vibrated.
The arrow quivered in the target.
Steady the camera before the shot.

items.meaning: a tremble in a sung note
items.example: The singer added vibrato to the long note.
items.exampleCN: 歌手在长音上加了颤音。

latinEntries.meaning: to shake, to quiver, to brandish

definition_zh: 恶习；邪恶；（机械）台钳；副职（前缀）
definition_en: a bad habit or immoral conduct, and, in compounds, a deputy
core_image: 老虎机旁的手一直不肯离开拉杆
scene: 社区讲座上，老师提醒家长别把赌博当成小事。The talk warned that gambling is a costly vice for many families.
sceneCN: 这里 vice 是「恶习」（第 1 个义项：不良的习惯或不道德的行为）；句意为讲座警告赌博是许多家庭负担沉重的恶习。老虎机旁不肯放手的那只手就是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 加后缀 -ious 构成，义为「凶恶的；恶毒的」
由 vicious 加 -ly 构成，义为「凶恶地」
拉丁短语，义为「反之亦然」

senses.title: A bad habit
senses.definition: a habit that is bad for the person who has it
senses.definitionCN: 对本人有害的习惯
senses.example: The talk warned that gambling is a vice that ruins families.
senses.exampleCN: 讲座警告赌博是一种毁掉家庭的恶习。
senses.why: Latin vitium named a flaw or a fault, and a habit can be exactly that.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vitium 指缺陷或过错，而习惯恰恰可能就是一个缺陷。

senses.title: Immoral conduct in general
senses.definition: wicked or immoral behaviour, especially in public life
senses.definitionCN: 尤其指公共生活中的邪恶或不道德行为
senses.example: The novel shows a city sinking into vice.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说写一座城市如何陷入堕落。
senses.why: A single flaw, repeated across a whole society, becomes a general word for wickedness.
senses.whyCN: 单个缺陷若在一整个社会反复出现，就成了泛指邪恶的词。

senses.title: A gripping tool on a workbench
senses.definition: a tool with two jaws that hold a piece of work
senses.definitionCN: 用两个钳口夹住工件的工作台工具
senses.example: Clamp the wood in a vice before you saw it.
senses.exampleCN: 锯之前先把木头夹在台钳里。
senses.why: The jaws of the tool close like a grip, and English borrowed the name from the same Latin word for a clamping device.
senses.whyCN: 钳口像握住一样合拢，英语从同一个表示夹持器具的拉丁词借来了这个名字。

senses.title: A deputy in a title
senses.definition: a person next in rank, used in compounds such as vice president
senses.definitionCN: 职级仅次于正职的人，用于 vice president 这类复合词中
senses.example: The vice president chaired the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 副总裁主持了会议。
senses.why: Latin vice meant in place of, so a vice president stands in place of the president.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vice 意为「代替」，所以 vice president 就是在总统（总裁）之时代行其职的人。

senses.title: A small weakness treated fondly
senses.definition: a small fault that people joke about rather than condemn
senses.definitionCN: 人们拿来打趣而不是谴责的小毛病
senses.example: Chocolate is my only vice.
senses.exampleCN: 巧克力是我唯一的嗜好。
senses.why: Once a moral word weakens, it can be used lightly about a harmless fondness.
senses.whyCN: 一个道德意味的词一旦变弱，就能轻松地用来指无伤大雅的偏好。

intro.en: Two Latin words lie behind vice: vitium, a fault, and vice, in place of.
intro.cn: vice 背后有两个拉丁词：vitium（过错）与 vice（代替）。

items.en: Vitium meant a defect, a fault, or a moral flaw.
items.cn: vitium 意为缺陷、过错或道德上的瑕疵。

items.en: French vice narrowed the word to a bad habit in daily life.
items.cn: 法语 vice 把词义收窄为日常生活中的恶习。

items.en: English used vice for a moral fault and for a gripping tool.
items.cn: 中世纪英语以 vice 既指道德上的过错，也指夹持的工具。

items.en: The separate Latin word vice meant in place of, as in vice consul.
items.cn: 另一个拉丁词 vice 意为「代替」，如 vice consul（副领事）。

items.en: Both strands meet in modern English: vice squad and vice president.
items.cn: 两支在现代英语里并存：vice squad（扫黄缉毒队）与 vice president（副总统）。

note.en: The first group holds the vice family, the second the moral words around it.
note.cn: 第一组是 vice 词族，第二组是围绕它的道德类词。

entries.definition: a suggestion about what to do
a wrong against a moral law
a point easily given in to

normalIntro.en: The bad habit and the deputy share a sound but not a history; keep the two strands apart.
normalIntro.cn: 「恶习」与「副职」读音相同却来源不同，要把两条线分开记。

normal.en: Advice and device contain vice by accident: they come from other roots.
normal.cn: advice 与 device 只是碰巧含 vice，来源不同。

normal.en: Vicious comes from vice, but a vice president does not.
normal.cn: vicious 来自「恶习」，vice president 则来自「代替」。

normal.en: A rule of thumb: vice before a title means deputy.
normal.cn: 一条经验：vice 放在头衔前就是「副」。

normal.en: The plural is vices, with the e kept.
normal.cn: 复数是 vices，保留 e。

normal.en: Latin vice meant in place of, as in vicarious.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 vice 意为代替，如 vicarious 一词中的含义。

abstract.en: See a hand that will not leave the lever of a slot machine.
abstract.cn: 想一只不肯离开老虎机拉杆的手。

abstract.en: Picture two steel jaws shutting on a plank.
abstract.cn: 想两个钢钳口夹住一块木板。

abstract.en: Think of a deputy who sits in the chief chair when the chief is away.
abstract.cn: 想一把手不在时坐在其位上的副手。

examples.en: Smoking is a vice many people struggle to give up.
examples.cn: 吸烟是许多人难以戒掉的恶习。

examples.en: She was appointed vice president of the company.
examples.cn: 她被任命为公司的副总裁。

examples.en: He fixed the shelf by holding the board in a vice.
examples.cn: 他用台钳夹住木板来修好了架子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「外死」——熬夜刷手机这习惯，把身体往外死拖，是明摆的恶习。

root: 拉丁语 vitium（缺陷）→ 法语 vice（恶习）；另拉丁语 vice（代替）→ vice president（副职）

sensesIntro.en: One short word holds a fault, a wicked city, a workbench clamp, a deputy, and a joke about chocolate.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个短词里装着过错、堕落的城市、台钳、副职，还有一句拿巧克力打趣的话。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand that cannot let go of a lever.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只放不下拉杆的手。

branches.en: The habit branch: gambling that ruins a family.
branches.cn: 习惯分支：毁掉家庭的赌博。

branches.en: The city branch: a town sinking into vice.
branches.cn: 城市分支：陷入堕落的小城。

branches.en: The bench branch: wood held in a vice.
branches.cn: 工作台分支：台钳夹住的木头。

branches.en: The deputy branch: the vice president in the chair.
branches.cn: 副职分支：坐在主位上的副总统。

branches.en: The joke branch: chocolate as my only vice.
branches.cn: 打趣分支：巧克力是我唯一的嗜好。

intro.en: The stem viti- (fault) built vicious; the separate Latin vice (in place of) built the deputy compounds.
intro.cn: 词干 viti-（过错）构成 vicious，另一个拉丁词 vice（代替）构成表副职的复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vitium and Latin vice look identical in English but are two different words with different relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vitium 与拉丁语 vice 在英语里写法相同，却是两个不同的词，亲属也不同。

items.example: Gambling is a vice.
Vicious means full of vice.
The dog growled viciously.
A vice consul stands below the consul.
Vice versa means the order is turned.
items.exampleCN: vice versa 意为顺序反过来了。

items.example: Virtue and vice are an old pair.
items.exampleCN: 善与恶是一对古老的搭配。

items.example: Device has no link to vice.
items.exampleCN: device 与 vice 没有词源关系。

items.example: Advice comes from a different root.
Debt can become a vicious circle.
items.exampleCN: 债务可能变成恶性循环。

latinEntries.meaning: a fault, a defect, a moral flaw

definition_en: to treat someone badly or unfairly, especially because of who they are
core_image: 一群人围着一个人，把过错全推到他身上
scene: 办公室里丢了钱，几个人不查清楚就把新来的实习生叫去问话。The older staff victimized the new intern over a missing wallet.
sceneCN: 这里 victimize 是「使受害、迫害」（第 1 个义项：因对方的身份或处境而恶意对待某人）；句意为老员工因一只不见的钱包就把新实习生当成了替罪羊。

derivatives.zh: 加后缀 -ization 构成，义为「受害；迫害」
加后缀 -er 构成，义为「迫害者」
去后缀 -ize 构成的名词，义为「受害者」

senses.title: To treat someone unfairly and make them suffer
senses.definition: to harm someone repeatedly or unfairly, often because they are weaker
senses.definitionCN: 因对方较弱或不同而反复不公地伤害某人
senses.example: The older staff victimized the new intern over a missing wallet.
senses.exampleCN: 老员工因一只不见的钱包就把新实习生当成了替罪羊。
senses.why: The verb takes the noun victim and adds the doing suffix -ize: to make a victim of someone.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词由名词 victim 加「使之」后缀 -ize 构成，即让某人成为受害者。

senses.title: To single people out for unequal treatment
senses.definition: to treat a group differently and worse than others in an official or everyday setting
senses.definitionCN: 在制度或日常场合中把某一群体区别对待得更差
senses.example: Employers who victimize older applicants face heavy fines.
senses.exampleCN: 歧视年长求职者的雇主会面临重罚。
senses.why: When unfairness follows a whole group rather than one person, the same verb names the practice.
senses.whyCN: 当不公针对的不是一个人而是一整个群体时，用的仍是这个动词。

senses.title: To make someone a victim on purpose
senses.definition: to cause someone to become a victim through a deliberate act
senses.definitionCN: 通过有意的行为使某人成为受害者
senses.example: The gang victimized shopkeepers who paid no protection money.
senses.exampleCN: 团伙把不交保护费的店主当成了整治对象。
senses.why: Any deliberate act that puts a person in the victim’s place fits the transitive verb.
senses.whyCN: 任何有意把人推到受害者位置上的行为，都符合这个及物动词的用法。

senses.title: To blame or punish someone for others’ faults
senses.definition: to make a person carry the blame or the cost of what others did
senses.definitionCN: 让别人承担他人行为造成的过错或代价
senses.example: Do not victimize the messenger for bad news.
senses.exampleCN: 不要因为坏消息就迁怒于报信的人。
senses.why: Blaming a bystander turns him into a victim even when no violence is involved.
senses.whyCN: 把责任推给旁观者，即使没有暴力，也把他变成了受害者。

senses.title: In law, to harm someone for reporting wrongdoing
senses.definition: to treat a person badly because they have complained, reported, or testified
senses.definitionCN: 因某人投诉、举报或作证而对其加以恶待
senses.example: The firm victimized the clerk who reported the safety fault.
senses.exampleCN: 公司报复了举报安全隐患的那名职员。
senses.why: Employment law needed a short verb for punishment that follows a complaint.
senses.whyCN: 劳动法需要一个简短动词来指投诉之后遭到的惩罚。

intro.en: Victimize is a modern formation: the noun victim plus the verb ending -ize.
intro.cn: victimize 是近代构词：名词 victim 加动词词尾 -ize。

items.en: Victima named a creature offered in sacrifice.
items.cn: victima 指用于献祭的活物。

items.en: French victime named the person destroyed by another.
items.cn: 法语 victime 指被他人毁灭的人。

items.en: The noun victim entered English and settled on the harmed party.
items.cn: 名词 victim 进入英语，固定在受损一方身上。

items.en: The suffix -ize, from Greek -izein through Latin, formed verbs meaning to make.
items.cn: -ize 词尾经拉丁语来自希腊语 -izein，构成「使之」类动词。

items.en: The verb victimize appeared in the nineteenth century, meaning to make a victim of.
items.cn: 动词 victimize 出现于十九世纪，义为「使某人成为受害者」。

note.en: The first group holds the victim family, the second lines up persecute, oppress, and the neutral harm.
note.cn: 第一组是 victim 词族，第二组排开 persecute、oppress 与中性的 harm。

entries.definition: to treat someone cruelly over time
to rule others harshly and unjustly

normalIntro.en: Add -ize to victim and the noun becomes an action: to put someone in the place of the harmed.
normalIntro.cn: victim 加 -ize，名词就成了动作：把人放进受害者的位置。

normal.en: Victimize, realize, and modernize all share the -ize ending.
normal.cn: victimize、realize、modernize 都共用 -ize 词尾。

normal.en: Victimization adds -ization, like realization.
normal.cn: victimization 加的是 -ization，如同 realization。

normal.en: The person who does it is the victimizer.
normal.cn: 施加迫害的人是 victimizer。

normal.en: Feel victimized is common in reports of unfair treatment.
normal.cn: 感到受了不公对待时常说 feel victimized。

normal.en: The stress stays on the first syllable: VIC-ti-mize.
normal.cn: 重音仍在第一音节：VIC-ti-mize。

abstract.en: Picture a group stepping back so one person falls.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人齐齐后退，让一个人摔下去。

abstract.en: See a name circled on a list while others are left alone.
abstract.cn: 想一张名单上只有一个名字被圈出来。

abstract.en: Hear a manager say the fault is always this worker’s.
abstract.cn: 听经理说，错总是这一个人的。

examples.en: The union says the company victimized workers who spoke up.
examples.cn: 工会称公司报复了敢于发声的工人。

examples.en: Children who are victimized at school often hide it.
examples.cn: 在学校受欺凌的孩子常把事瞒着。

examples.en: No law lets an employer victimize a pregnant applicant.
examples.cn: 没有任何法律允许雇主歧视怀孕的求职者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「维克厅埋子」——维克厅为了掩盖旧事，把知情的孩子迫害了。

root: 拉丁语 victima（献祭的活物）→ 法语 victime → victim + -ize（使…）→ victimize

sensesIntro.en: One verb covers unfair treatment of a person, of a group, of a scapegoat, and of anyone punished for speaking out.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个动词覆盖了对个人、对群体、对替罪者，以及对举报者的不公对待。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crowd pushing the blame onto one person.
core.cn: 核心意象：一群人把过错推给一个人。

branches.en: The unfair branch: staff turning on an intern.
branches.cn: 不公分支：员工一同针对实习生。

branches.en: The group branch: older applicants shut out.
branches.cn: 群体分支：年长求职者被拒。

branches.en: The gang branch: shopkeepers picked as targets.
branches.cn: 团伙分支：店主被当作目标。

branches.en: The scapegoat branch: blaming the messenger.
branches.cn: 替罪分支：迁怒报信人。

branches.en: The law branch: payback for a report.
branches.cn: 法律分支：因举报而遭报复。

intro.en: The stem victim- plus the verb suffix -ize yields the base verb; -ization, -er, and -less extend the family.
intro.cn: 词干 victim- 加动词后缀 -ize 构成基础动词，再以 -ization、-er、-less 扩展词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin victima has no clear relatives; the productive suffix -ize is what gives the word its action.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 victima 缺乏明确亲缘，真正赋予动作义的是能产后缀 -ize。

items.example: Victim- is the base of the family.
items.exampleCN: victim- 是这个词族的词基。

items.example: Victimize means to make a victim.
items.exampleCN: victimize 意为使某人成为受害者。

items.example: Victimization names the practice.
A victimizer acts on others.
A victimless crime has no harmed party.
items.exampleCN: 无受害者犯罪没有受损一方。

items.example: The victimized clerk was moved to another office.
items.exampleCN: 被报复的职员被调到另一间办公室。

items.example: Persecute stresses a campaign.
items.exampleCN: persecute 强调持续追打的运动。

items.example: Oppress stresses the weight of power.
The law exists to protect, not to victimize.
items.exampleCN: 法律的存在是为了保护，而不是使人受害。

definition_en: success in a contest, battle, or struggle against an opponent or a difficulty
core_image: 终场哨响，全队抱在一起跳起来
scene: 决赛最后一分钟，主队攻入一球，看台上的人全都站了起来。The home side celebrated a narrow victory over the champions.
sceneCN: 这里 victory 是「胜利」（第 1 个义项：在比赛、战斗或与对手、困难的较量中取得胜利）；句意为主队在主场以微弱优势战胜了冠军队。终场哨响时抱在一起的人就是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 加后缀 -ious 构成，义为「胜利的；获胜的」
加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「胜利地」
同源名词，义为「胜利者」

senses.title: Success in a contest or battle
senses.definition: the act of defeating an opponent in a game, fight, or war
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛、战斗或战争中击败对手
senses.example: The home side celebrated a narrow victory over the champions.
senses.exampleCN: 主队庆祝以微弱优势战胜了冠军队。
senses.why: Latin victoria came from victor, the winner, and a winner is what a contest produces.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 victoria 来自 victor（胜者），而胜者正是竞争产生的结果。

senses.title: Success in a struggle against difficulty
senses.definition: success in overcoming a problem, illness, or obstacle
senses.definitionCN: 克服问题、疾病或障碍而取得成功
senses.example: Her recovery was a quiet victory over fear.
senses.exampleCN: 她的康复是一场无声的、战胜恐惧的胜利。
senses.why: The opponent need not be a person: a disease or a fear can be beaten too.
senses.whyCN: 对手不必是人：疾病、恐惧同样可以被战胜。

senses.title: An advantage gained for a cause
senses.definition: a result that proves right or helps a principle or group
senses.definitionCN: 证明某一主张正确、或有利于某一原则与群体的结果
senses.example: The ruling is a victory for press freedom.
senses.exampleCN: 这一裁定是新闻自由的胜利。
senses.why: When a court or an election settles a principle, the side that principle favours has won.
senses.whyCN: 当法院或选举就某原则定论时，该原则所支持的一方就等于获胜。

senses.title: In ancient use, the goddess of success
senses.definition: the Roman goddess who personified success
senses.definitionCN: 古罗马象征成功的女神维多利亚
senses.example: A statue of Victory stood at the head of the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 大厅一端立着一尊胜利女神像。
senses.why: Rome turned abstract success into a goddess, and her name is this noun.
senses.whyCN: 古罗马把抽象的成功人格化为女神，女神的名称正是这个词。

senses.title: The moment of triumph in speech or writing
senses.definition: a report or celebration of a win, as in headlines
senses.definitionCN: 对胜利的报道或庆祝，如新闻标题中的用法
senses.example: News of the victory reached the capital by noon.
senses.exampleCN: 胜利的消息中午就传到了首都。
senses.why: Once news travels, the abstract win becomes a piece of news people pass on.
senses.whyCN: 消息一旦传开，抽象的胜利就成了一条被人们转述的新闻。

intro.en: Victory goes back to Latin victoria, from victor, the one who wins.
intro.cn: victory 追溯至拉丁语 victoria，来自 victor（胜者）。

items.en: Vincere meant to conquer, and victor named the one who conquered.
items.cn: vincere 意为征服，victor 指征服者。

items.en: Victoria was the abstract noun for the win itself, and also a goddess.
items.cn: victoria 既是「胜利」这一抽象名词，也是一位女神。

items.en: French victoire carried the word toward English.
items.cn: 法语 victoire 把该词带向英语。

items.en: English took victory for a win in battle or in argument.
items.cn: 中世纪英语以 victory 指战斗或辩论中的胜利。

items.en: Sport and politics widened it to games, elections, and moral causes.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到比赛、选举与道义主张。

note.en: The first group holds the victor family, the second the close words for winning and losing.
note.cn: 第一组是 victor 词族，第二组是表示胜负的相近词。

entries.definition: the taking of land by force

normalIntro.en: From the Latin goddess of success to the final score of a match: victory always ends a contest.
normalIntro.cn: 从拉丁语的成功女神到比赛的最终比分：victory 总在为一场较量收尾。

normal.en: Victory and victim look alike but have no common Latin root.
normal.cn: victory 与 victim 形似，却没有共同的拉丁词根。

normal.en: Drop the -y and add -or for victor, the winner.
normal.cn: 去掉 -y 加 -or 即 victor，获胜的人。

normal.en: Victorious adds -ious, like glorious.
normal.cn: victorious 加 -ious，如同 glorious。

normal.en: The plural changes y to ies: victories.
normal.cn: 复数 y 变 ies：victories。

normal.en: V is the sign of the Roman victory goddess on coins.
normal.cn: 古罗马钱币上的 V 就是胜利女神的标记。

abstract.en: See the scoreboard freeze at one goal ahead.
abstract.cn: 想记分牌定格在领先一球。

abstract.en: Hear a whole stand breathe out at the final whistle.
abstract.cn: 听终场哨响时整片看台一起呼气。

abstract.en: Picture a stone goddess with wings at the hall door.
abstract.cn: 想大厅门口一尊带翅膀的石女神。

examples.en: The team has now won three victories in a row.
examples.cn: 这支队伍如今已连赢三场。

examples.en: The law was seen as a victory for small farmers.
examples.cn: 这项法律被视为小农的胜利。

examples.en: They claimed victory before all the votes were counted.
examples.cn: 票还没数完他们就宣布获胜了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「维克多利」——维克多力气最大，比赛拿了第一，胜利归他。

root: 拉丁语 vincere（征服）→ victor（胜者）→ victoria（胜利）→ 法语 victoire → 英语 victory

sensesIntro.en: One noun runs from a battle won, through a fear overcome and a principle upheld, to a goddess and a headline.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个名词从打赢一场仗，延伸到战胜恐惧、捍卫原则，再延伸到女神与新闻标题。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a team leaping together as the whistle blows.
core.cn: 核心意象：终场哨响时全队一起跃起。

branches.en: The match branch: a narrow win at home.
branches.cn: 比赛分支：主场的险胜。

branches.en: The illness branch: a quiet win over fear.
branches.cn: 疾病分支：战胜恐惧的无声胜利。

branches.en: The cause branch: a ruling for press freedom.
branches.cn: 主张分支：有利于新闻自由的裁定。

branches.en: The altar branch: the winged goddess on her pedestal.
branches.cn: 神坛分支：柱座上的带翅膀女神。

branches.en: The news branch: word of the win reaching the capital.
branches.cn: 新闻分支：捷报传至首都。

intro.en: The root vinc-, vict- means to conquer; -or, -ory, and -ious build the family.
intro.cn: 词根 vinc-、vict- 意为征服，-or、-ory、-ious 构成这个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin vincere gave victor and victoria; the stem vict- carries the sense of overcoming into every English form.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vincere 派生 victor 与 victoria，词干 vict- 把「克服」之义带进每个英语形式。

items.example: Vict- carries the sense of winning.
A victor is the one who wins.
Victory names the state of having won.
items.exampleCN: victory 指已经获胜的状态。

items.example: Victorious means full of the win.
items.exampleCN: victorious 意为充满胜利感的。

items.example: They marched victoriously into the square.
The season brought six victories.
items.exampleCN: 这个赛季带来六场胜利。

items.example: The triumph was marked by a parade.
items.exampleCN: 以游行的方式庆祝这次凯旋。

items.example: Defeat taught them more than victory.
items.exampleCN: 失败教会他们的比胜利更多。

items.example: Convince shares the winning root.

definition_en: a recording of moving images, or the medium that carries them
core_image: 手机屏幕上，一段画面正在播放
scene: 面试前她对着手机录了一段自我介绍，反复看了三遍才发出去。She recorded a short video to introduce herself before the interview.
sceneCN: 这里 video 是「视频、录像」（第 1 个义项：由连续画面构成的影像作品）；句意为面试前她录了一小段视频介绍自己。手机屏幕上正在播放的画面正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 合成词，义为「录像带」
合成词，义为「可视电话」
加后缀 -graphy 构成，义为「摄像；录像制作」

senses.title: A recording of moving pictures
senses.definition: a length of recorded moving images, with or without sound
senses.definitionCN: 一段录下的连续画面，可有声音也可无声
senses.example: She recorded a short video to introduce herself before the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 面试前她录了一小段视频介绍自己。
senses.why: Latin video means I see; a recording lets you see again what passed in front of a lens.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 video 意为「我看见」；录像让你再次看见曾经经过镜头的东西。

senses.title: The medium or signal that carries moving pictures
senses.definition: the system, signal, or equipment used to record and show moving images
senses.definitionCN: 用于录制和显示活动影像的系统、信号或设备
senses.example: The lecture was sent to remote students by video.
senses.exampleCN: 这堂课通过视频传给远端的学生。
senses.why: A recording is a thing; the channel that carries it is also called video, as in by video.
senses.whyCN: 录像是一个实物，而承载它的渠道也叫 video，如 by video。

senses.title: Short internet clips and their culture
senses.definition: a short clip made for online sharing, and the stream of such clips
senses.definitionCN: 为网络分享而制作的短片，以及这类内容的整体
senses.example: He spends an hour on short videos every night.
senses.exampleCN: 他每晚都刷一小时短视频。
senses.why: Once clips could be shared in seconds, the word grew into a genre of its own.
senses.whyCN: 短片可以秒速分享之后，这个词发展成了一个独立的内容类别。

senses.title: To record moving images
senses.definition: to make a recording of moving images with a camera or phone
senses.definitionCN: 用摄像机或手机录制活动影像
senses.example: They videoed the whole ceremony on a phone.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用手机把整个仪式都录了下来。
senses.why: Nouns turn into verbs easily in English, and video became one: to video an event.
senses.whyCN: 英语里名词容易转成动词，video 也是如此：把一场活动录下来。

senses.title: In teaching, visual material as a channel
senses.definition: recorded visual material used to teach or demonstrate
senses.definitionCN: 用于教学或示范的录制影像材料
senses.example: The course adds video to every unit.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课每个单元都加入影像材料。
senses.why: Classrooms borrow the word to name visual material that supports a lesson.
senses.whyCN: 课堂借用这个词来称呼辅助教学的影像材料。

intro.en: Video is a modern word taken straight from the Latin verb video, I see.
intro.cn: video 是近代直接取自拉丁动词 video（我看见）的词。

items.en: Videre meant to see, and video is its first person, I see.
items.cn: videre 意为看见，video 是它的第一人称形式「我看见」。

items.en: The Latin phrase video et taceo, I see and keep silent, shows the verb in use.
items.cn: 拉丁语短语 video et taceo（我看见而不语）正是该动词的用例。

items.en: Technical writers of the twentieth century used Latin stems for new media.
items.cn: 二十世纪的技术作者用拉丁词干给新媒介命名。

items.en: Video, from Latin through the sense of seeing, was coined against audio, I hear.
items.cn: video 与表示听见的 audio 相对，借「看见」之义造出。

items.en: It moved from equipment to recording to clips, and then to a verb.
items.cn: 它从设备转到录像，又转到短片，最后成为动词。

note.en: The first group holds compounds built on video, the second the media that compete with it.
note.cn: 第一组是由 video 构成的合成词，第二组是与视频并列的媒介。

entries.definition: a phone that shows the caller
a short piece of a recording
a long recorded story on screen

normalIntro.en: Latin video, I see, is the whole story: whatever lets you see again is called video.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁语 video（我看见）就是全部由来：凡是让你再看一遍的东西，都叫 video。

normal.en: Video and audio are a pair: I see against I hear.
normal.cn: video 与 audio 是一对：我看见对我听见。

normal.en: The plural is videos, plainly adding s.
normal.cn: 复数 videos，直接加 s。

normal.en: As a verb it takes -ed: they videoed the event.
normal.cn: 作动词时加 -ed：they videoed the event。

normal.en: Video calling keeps the noun before another noun.
normal.cn: video calling 是名词作定语。

normal.en: The Latin verb videre also gives visible and vision.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 videre 还派生 visible 与 vision。

abstract.en: See a small screen in a hand, a face speaking.
abstract.cn: 想手心里的小屏幕里有一张脸在说话。

abstract.en: Hear the click of a record button.
abstract.cn: 听录制键按下的一声轻响。

abstract.en: Picture a lens and an eye drawn side by side.
abstract.cn: 想一枚镜头和一只眼睛并排放着。

examples.en: The school posted a video of the concert online.
examples.cn: 学校把音乐会的视频发到了网上。

examples.en: Please video the meeting so absent staff can watch.
examples.cn: 请把会议录下来，好让缺席的同事观看。

examples.en: Video has largely replaced tape in newsrooms.
examples.cn: 在新闻编辑室里，视频已基本取代了磁带。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂迪欧」——喂，迪欧，快把刚才那一段录像发给我。

root: 拉丁语 videre（看见）的第一人称 video（我看见）→ 英语 video

sensesIntro.en: From a single Latin sentence, I see, the word grew into recordings, signals, online clips, a verb, and classroom material.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一句拉丁语「我看见」出发，这个词扩展成录像、信号、网络短片、动词与课堂材料。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: moving pictures playing on a phone screen.
core.cn: 核心意象：手机屏幕上播放的活动画面。

branches.en: The recording branch: a self-introduction filmed at home.
branches.cn: 录像分支：家里录的自我介绍。

branches.en: The signal branch: a lecture sent by video.
branches.cn: 信号分支：靠视频传送的课。

branches.en: The feed branch: an hour of short clips.
branches.cn: 信息流分支：刷一小时的短片。

branches.en: The camera branch: filming the whole ceremony.
branches.cn: 镜头分支：录下整场仪式。

branches.en: The classroom branch: video added to a unit.
branches.cn: 课堂分支：单元里加入影像。

intro.en: The Latin root vid-, vis- means to see; video is the bare verb form used as a noun.
intro.cn: 拉丁词根 vid-、vis- 意为看见，video 是直接用作名词的动词形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre, to see, gives video, visible, vision, and television; the root appears whole in this word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre（看见）派生 video、visible、vision、television，本词中词根完整呈现。

items.example: Vid- means seeing in video.
items.exampleCN: vid- 在 video 中意为看见。

items.example: Video is literally I see.
Videotape joined video with tape.
items.exampleCN: videotape 由 video 与 tape 合成。

items.example: A videophone shows the speaker.
Videography names the craft.
Two videos were uploaded.
They videoed the talk.
Visible shares the seeing root.
Audio is the hearing partner of video.
items.exampleCN: audio 是 video 的听觉对应词。

definition_en: what can be seen from a place, or the way a person thinks about something
core_image: 推开旅馆的窗，整片湖面铺在眼前
scene: 旅馆房间在六楼，她拉开窗帘，整片湖面就铺在眼前。The room has a fine view of the lake and the hills behind it.
sceneCN: 这里 view 是「景色」（第 1 个义项：从某处能看到的景象）；句意为这个房间能看到湖与湖后群山的好景色。推开窗后铺开的画面正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 加后缀 -er 构成，义为「观众；观看者」
合成词，义为「观点；视角」
加前缀 re- 构成，义为「回顾；评论」

senses.title: What can be seen from a place
senses.definition: the whole scene that a place allows you to see
senses.definitionCN: 从某一位置能看到的整体景象
senses.example: The room has a fine view of the lake and the hills behind it.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间能看到湖与湖后群山的好景色。
senses.why: To look out is to see; the scene laid before the eyes is the view.
senses.whyCN: 向外看是「看」这个动作，而铺在眼前的那片景象就是 view。

senses.title: A person’s opinion about something
senses.definition: a particular way of thinking about a matter
senses.definitionCN: 对某事的特定想法
senses.example: In my view the plan costs too much.
senses.exampleCN: 在我看来这个计划花费太高。
senses.why: The eye and the mind use one word: what you see from where you stand is what you think from where you stand.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛与头脑共用一个词：从哪个位置看，就从哪个位置想。

senses.title: The range within which something can be seen
senses.definition: the area that can be seen from a point, or the chance to see something
senses.definitionCN: 从一个位置能看见的区域，或看见某物的机会
senses.example: The ship came into view at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 黎明时那艘船出现在视野里。
senses.why: A view is not only the picture but the space in which the picture can appear.
senses.whyCN: view 不只是那幅画面，也是画面得以出现的空间。

senses.title: To look at something carefully
senses.definition: to watch or examine something, especially for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 有目的地观看或检查某物
senses.example: The committee viewed the site before voting.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会在表决前察看了现场。
senses.why: The noun gives a verb: to give a thing your view is to view it.
senses.whyCN: 名词派生动词：把目光给某物，就是去观看它。

senses.title: To regard something in a certain way
senses.definition: to think of something as being a particular thing
senses.definitionCN: 把某物视为某一性质的事物
senses.example: Many people view silence as agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 很多人把沉默看作同意。
senses.why: When the mind places a thing before itself, the same verb names the judgment.
senses.whyCN: 当头脑把一物摆在自身之前端详时，这个动词也用来表示判断。

senses.title: What can be seen in a picture or on a screen
senses.definition: the scene shown in an image, drawing, or display
senses.definitionCN: 图像、图画或屏幕中显示的场景
senses.example: The drawing shows the house from the front view.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅画从正面视角画了这座房子。
senses.why: Images repeat the word, naming the angle from which a scene is drawn.
senses.whyCN: 图像沿用了这个词，用来指画面取景的角度。

intro.en: View comes from Old French veue, a seeing, from Latin videre, to see.
intro.cn: view 来自古法语 veue（看见），源头是拉丁语 videre（看）。

items.en: Videre meant to see, and its past participle visus gave the noun of seeing.
items.cn: videre 意为看见，其过去分词 visus 派生出「所见」的名词。

items.en: French veue named the act of seeing and the sight itself.
items.cn: 法语 veue 既指看的动作，也指所见之物。

items.en: English borrowed it as vewe, later spelled view.
items.cn: 英语借入作 vewe，后来拼作 view。

items.en: The sense widened from sight to the scene before the eyes.
items.cn: 词义从「看」扩展到眼前的景象。

items.en: Opinion and examination joined the family, giving in my view and to view a site.
items.cn: 「看法」与「检查」加入词族，产生 in my view 与 view a site。

note.en: The first group holds words built on view, the second the words for scenes and opinions.
note.cn: 第一组是由 view 构成的词，第二组是表示景象与看法的词。

entries.definition: a position from which one thinks
the power or act of seeing
a broad look over an area

normalIntro.en: Latin to see becomes both the thing seen and the thought held: the eye and the mind share one short word.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「看」既成为所见之物，也成为所持之见：眼睛与头脑共用一个短词。

normal.en: View is short but the vowel is long: /vjuː/.
normal.cn: view 拼写不长，但元音读长音 /vjuː/。

normal.en: Viewer adds -er for the one watching.
normal.cn: viewer 加 -er 表示观看的人。

normal.en: Viewpoint joins view and point, a place to think from.
normal.cn: viewpoint 由 view 与 point 合成，指思考所站的位置。

normal.en: Review begins with re-, to look again.
normal.cn: review 以 re- 开头，意为再看一遍。

normal.en: In my view is the standard way to give an opinion.
normal.cn: 给出看法时常用 in my view。

abstract.en: See curtains pulled back onto a wide lake.
abstract.cn: 想窗帘被拉开，露出一整片湖。

abstract.en: Picture two people on one hill looking different ways.
abstract.cn: 想一座山上两个人朝不同方向看。

abstract.en: Hear someone say that is how I see it.
abstract.cn: 听有人说，我就是这么看的。

examples.en: From the top of the tower the whole town is in view.
examples.cn: 从塔顶望去，整座小镇尽收眼底。

examples.en: The council viewed the plans with suspicion.
examples.cn: 议会带着怀疑看待这些计划。

examples.en: Her view of the matter changed after the meeting.
examples.cn: 会议之后，她对这件事的看法变了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「V 呦」——站在山顶比个 V，呦，风景真好看。

root: 拉丁语 videre（看见）→ 过去分词 visus → 古法语 veue → 英语 view

sensesIntro.en: The word starts with a scene from a window and ends with a judgment in the mind; the verb bridges watching and regarding.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从窗外的景象开始，走到心中的判断；动词则连接了「观看」与「看作」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lake spread out beyond an open window.
core.cn: 核心意象：敞开的窗外铺开一片湖。

branches.en: The window branch: lake and hills from a room.
branches.cn: 窗户分支：房里望见的湖与山。

branches.en: The opinion branch: my view on the cost.
branches.cn: 看法分支：我对花费的看法。

branches.en: The range branch: a ship heaving into sight.
branches.cn: 范围分支：船驶入视野。

branches.en: The looking branch: viewing a site, and viewing silence as consent.
branches.cn: 观看分支：察看现场，把沉默看作同意。

branches.en: The drawing branch: a house shown from the front view.
branches.cn: 绘图分支：房子的正面视图。

intro.en: The root vid-, vis-, view- means to see; -er, -point, and re- extend the word.
intro.cn: 词根 vid-、vis-、view- 意为看见，-er、-point、re- 扩展这个词。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre, to see, passed through French as veue and reaches English as view, with its relatives visible and vision.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre（看见）经法语 veue 传入英语成为 view，同族还有 visible 与 vision。

items.example: View carries the seeing root.
A viewer watches a programme.
A viewpoint is where one stands to think.
items.exampleCN: viewpoint 是思考所站的位置。

items.example: Review means to see again.
Preview shows the work before release.
items.exampleCN: preview 在上映前展示作品。

items.example: Their views differ.
The board viewed the report.
Visible shares the root vis-.
items.exampleCN: visible 与词根 vis- 同源。

items.example: Vision also comes from videre.

definition_en: a way of thinking about something, or a position from which something is seen
core_image: 两个人在山的两侧，看到不同的坡
scene: 讨论会上，工程师和村民对同一个水坝各说各话，因为他们的立场完全不同。From a farmer’s viewpoint, the dam is a threat rather than a promise.
sceneCN: 这里 viewpoint 是「观点、立场」（第 1 个义项：思考某事时所处的角度）；句意为从农民的角度看，这座水坝是威胁而非希望。山两侧看到不同坡面的两个人正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 合成词的前半部分，义为「看法；景色」
合成词的后半部分，义为「点；位置」
加后缀 -ed 构成，义为「带有特定立场的」（少数用法）

senses.title: A way of thinking about a matter
senses.definition: a particular attitude or set of opinions on a subject
senses.definitionCN: 对某一问题所持的态度或一套看法
senses.example: From a farmer’s viewpoint, the dam is a threat rather than a promise.
senses.exampleCN: 从农民的角度看，这座水坝是威胁而非希望。
senses.why: View gives what one sees and point gives where one stands; together they name the place a judgment comes from.
senses.whyCN: view 给的是所见，point 给的是所站之处；合起来就指判断出自的那个位置。

senses.title: A physical position for observing
senses.definition: the spot from which a scene or object is looked at
senses.definitionCN: 观看某一场景或物体时所处的地点
senses.example: The guide marked the best viewpoint above the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 导游标出了山谷上方最好的观景位置。
senses.why: A painter must choose an eye-level before starting, and that place is literally a viewpoint.
senses.whyCN: 画家动笔前要选定视平线所在的位置，那正是字面意义上的 viewpoint。

senses.title: The angle shown in a picture or film
senses.definition: the camera angle from which a scene is filmed or drawn
senses.definitionCN: 拍摄或绘制场景时所用的机位角度
senses.example: The scene is shot from a child’s viewpoint.
senses.exampleCN: 这场戏是从一个孩子的视角拍的。
senses.why: Film borrows the word to name the eye the camera pretends to be.
senses.whyCN: 电影借用这个词，指镜头假装成为的那只眼睛。

senses.title: In debate, one side of an argument
senses.definition: one of the positions presented in a discussion or dispute
senses.definitionCN: 讨论或争执中所呈现的一个立场
senses.example: Each viewpoint was given ten minutes in the debate.
senses.exampleCN: 辩论中每一方立场各给十分钟。
senses.why: When positions are counted and timed, the abstract angle becomes a labelled side.
senses.whyCN: 当各方立场被计数并分配时间时，抽象的角度就成了一条标名的立场。

senses.title: A standpoint supported by evidence
senses.definition: an opinion backed by facts or experience rather than feeling
senses.definitionCN: 以事实或经验为依据而非仅凭感觉的意见
senses.example: Her viewpoint rests on five years of field data.
senses.exampleCN: 她的看法建立在五年实地数据之上。
senses.why: The word suits arguments that can point at something, since point is inside it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词适合能指向具体证据的论证，因为它本身就含着 point。

intro.en: Viewpoint is an English compound: view, what is seen, plus point, a place.
intro.cn: viewpoint 是英语合成词：view（所见）加 point（位置）。

items.en: Veue, a seeing, reached English as view.
items.cn: 古法语 veue（看见）进入英语成为 view。

items.en: Punctum meant a small hole or a dot, from pungere, to prick.
items.cn: punctum 意为小孔或小点，源自 pungere（刺）。

items.en: French point named a dot or a place on a surface.
items.cn: 法语 point 指平面上的点或位置。

items.en: The compound viewpoint joined the two words for a judging position.
items.cn: 合成词 viewpoint 把两个词合成表示判断的位置。

items.en: It spread from painting and surveying to opinion writing.
items.cn: 它从绘画与测量扩展到议论文章。

note.en: The first group holds the two words that make the compound plus its relatives, the second the near synonyms for opinion.
note.cn: 第一组是构成这个合成词的两个词及相近形式，第二组是「意见」的近义词。

entries.definition: the position from which one judges
a way of seeing things in proportion
the direction from which a thing is approached

normalIntro.en: Two plain words welded together: where you view from is what you point at.
normalIntro.cn: 两个普通词焊在一起：从哪里看，就指向什么。

normal.en: Viewpoint is view plus point, and the stress falls on view.
normal.cn: viewpoint 是 view 加 point，重音落在 view。

normal.en: Standpoint is its close twin, made with stand.
normal.cn: standpoint 是它的近义双胞胎，用 stand 构成。

normal.en: It takes from: from my viewpoint.
normal.cn: 前面常接 from：from my viewpoint。

normal.en: The plural simply adds s: viewpoints.
normal.cn: 复数直接加 s：viewpoints。

normal.en: Point at the end hints that reasons can be pointed to.
normal.cn: 结尾的 point 提示理由是可以指出的。

abstract.en: Picture two hikers on opposite slopes, each seeing one side.
abstract.cn: 想两位徒步者站在山坡两侧，各看见一面。

abstract.en: See a camera lowered to a child’s height.
abstract.cn: 想镜头降到孩子的高度。

abstract.en: Hear a speaker say, from where I stand.
abstract.cn: 听人说我站的位置看到的是这样。

examples.en: The article presents the viewpoint of the workers, not the owners.
examples.cn: 这篇文章呈现的是工人的立场，而不是雇主的。

examples.en: Seen from a historical viewpoint, the treaty looks different.
examples.cn: 从历史的视角看，这份条约大不相同。

examples.en: The hilltop is the best viewpoint in the park.
examples.cn: 山顶是公园里最好的观景点。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「唯一炮硬」——只有一门炮硬说有理，这就是他的观点。

root: view（看法，源自拉丁 videre「看」）+ point（点，源自拉丁 punctum）→ viewpoint

sensesIntro.en: A seeing plus a place gives a word that covers opinions, camera angles, and the hilltop where you stand to look.
sensesIntro.cn: 「看」加上「位置」，合成一个同时覆盖意见、机位与山顶观景处的词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people on opposite slopes of one hill.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一座山两侧的两个人。

branches.en: The farmer branch: a dam seen as a threat.
branches.cn: 农民分支：水坝被视为威胁。

branches.en: The hilltop branch: the best place to look down.
branches.cn: 山顶分支：俯瞰的最佳位置。

branches.en: The camera branch: a scene at a child’s height.
branches.cn: 镜头分支：孩子高度的场景。

branches.en: The debate branch: ten minutes for each side.
branches.cn: 辩论分支：每方十分钟。

branches.en: The evidence branch: five years of field data.
branches.cn: 证据分支：五年的实地数据。

intro.en: Viewpoint is built from two free words, view and point, each with its own Latin root.
intro.cn: viewpoint 由两个自由词 view 与 point 构成，各自有自己的拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: Videre, to see, supplies view; punctum, a dot, supplies point; English merely joints them.
latinIntro.cn: videre（看见）提供 view，punctum（点）提供 point，英语只是把二者拼合。

items.example: View comes from Latin videre.
Point comes from Latin punctum.
The second half fixes the place.
Several viewpoints were recorded.
A viewpointed essay takes a clear side.
items.exampleCN: 有立场的文章总会偏向一方。

items.example: Standpoint is built the same way.
Perspective comes from per and specere.
items.exampleCN: perspective 来自 per 与 specere。

items.example: Outlook looks outward for a general view.
items.exampleCN: outlook 向外看，指总体看法。

definition_zh: 精力充沛的；有力的；强健的
definition_en: full of physical strength and energy, or strong and forceful
core_image: 晨跑的人大步跨过台阶，呼吸深而稳
scene: 医生看完体检报告，说他恢复得很好，可以恢复剧烈运动了。The doctor said he could return to vigorous exercise.
sceneCN: 这里 vigorous 是「剧烈的、有力的」（第 2 个义项：强度大而有力量）；句意为医生说他可以恢复剧烈运动了。大步跨台阶、呼吸深稳的晨跑者就是这个词给人的感觉。

pos.zh: 精力充沛的；有力的；强健的

derivatives.zh: 去后缀构成名词，义为「精力；活力」（美式 vigor）
加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「有力地；精力充沛地」
加前缀 in- 与后缀 -ate 构成，义为「使振奋；使有活力」

senses.title: Full of bodily strength
senses.definition: strong, healthy, and full of energy
senses.definitionCN: 强壮、健康且充满活力
senses.example: At seventy he is still vigorous and walks five miles a day.
senses.exampleCN: 他七十岁仍精力充沛，每天走五英里。
senses.why: Latin vigor meant liveliness and force, and a vigorous person carries both.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vigor 意为活力与力量，精力充沛的人两者兼有。

senses.title: Strong in force or intensity
senses.definition: done with great force or energy
senses.definitionCN: 以很大力量或强度完成的
senses.example: The doctor said he could return to vigorous exercise.
senses.exampleCN: 医生说他可以恢复剧烈运动了。
senses.why: The same force, applied to an activity rather than a person, makes the activity vigorous.
senses.whyCN: 同一股力量若落到活动上而非人身上，活动本身就变得有力、剧烈。

senses.title: Lively and forceful in speech or style
senses.definition: expressed with energy and confidence
senses.definitionCN: 表达得充满能量与自信
senses.example: She made a vigorous defence of the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 她为这项计划做了有力的辩护。
senses.why: Language borrows the body and puts its force into argument.
senses.whyCN: 语言借用身体的力量，把它注入论辩之中。

senses.title: Growing strongly
senses.definition: growing fast and healthily, as a plant does
senses.definitionCN: 像植物那样快速而健康地生长
senses.example: Vigorous growth followed the spring rain.
senses.exampleCN: 春雨之后出现了旺盛的生长。
senses.why: What is strong in body is active in growth as well.
senses.whyCN: 强健之物在生长上也同样有劲。

senses.title: Energetic in a public effort
senses.definition: carried out with much energy by a group
senses.definitionCN: 由一个群体以大量精力开展的
senses.example: The city ran a vigorous campaign against litter.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市开展了声势浩大的反乱扔垃圾运动。
senses.why: A group with vigour turns it into a movement.
senses.whyCN: 一个有活力的群体，会把它变成一场运动。

intro.en: Vigorous rests on Latin vigor, the liveliness that makes a body act.
intro.cn: vigorous 建立在拉丁语 vigor 之上，指让身体动起来的那股活劲。

items.en: Vigere meant to be lively or to flourish, and vigor was that liveliness.
items.cn: vigere 意为有生机、繁茂，vigor 即那股生机。

items.en: French vigour carried the word with the sense of strength.
items.cn: 法语 vigour 带着「力量」的含义承接此词。

items.en: English vigour named bodily force and the force of law alike.
items.cn: 中世纪英语 vigour 既指体力，也指法律的效力。

items.en: The adjective vigorous spread to exercise, argument, and growth.
items.cn: 形容词 vigorous 扩展到运动、论辩与生长。

items.en: American spelling drops the u: vigor, but keeps vigorous.
items.cn: 美式拼写去掉 u 作 vigor，但 vigorous 不变。

note.en: The first group holds the vigour family, the second the words for strength and its lack.
note.cn: 第一组是 vigour 词族，第二组是力量及其缺乏的表达。

normalIntro.en: Vigour is the noun, vigorous the adjective, and in- can hand the energy out again.
normalIntro.cn: vigour 是名词，vigorous 是形容词，加上 in- 就能把能量再分给别人。

normal.en: Vigour plus -ous gives vigorous, as if full of vigour.
normal.cn: vigour 加 -ous 得 vigorous，意为充满活力。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with rigorous, which means strict.
normal.cn: 别与 rigorous（严格的）混淆。

normal.en: American English writes vigor but still writes vigorous.
normal.cn: 美式写作 vigor，但形容词仍是 vigorous。

normal.en: Invigorate means to put vigour into someone.
normal.cn: invigorate 意为把活力注入某人。

normal.en: Latin vigere, to flourish, also hides in vigil, a night watch.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 vigere（繁茂）也藏在 vigil（守夜）里。

abstract.en: See a runner taking the steps two at a time.
abstract.cn: 想跑者一次跨两级台阶。

abstract.en: Feel a deep, steady breath after a hard climb.
abstract.cn: 感受费力爬坡后深而稳的呼吸。

abstract.en: Watch a young shoot push up fast after rain.
abstract.cn: 看雨后新芽猛地往上蹿。

examples.en: She is a vigorous campaigner for cleaner air.
examples.cn: 她是一位为更清洁空气奔走的活动家。

examples.en: The plants showed vigorous growth in warm weather.
examples.cn: 天气温暖时植株生长旺盛。

examples.en: He shook my hand in a vigorous grip.
examples.cn: 他有力地握住我的手摇了摇。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威哥热死」——威哥热得满头汗还跑第一，精力不是一般的充沛。

root: 拉丁语 vigere（有生机；繁茂）→ vigor（活力）→ 法语 vigour → 英语 vigorous

sensesIntro.en: One Latin word for liveliness spreads from a strong body to strong exercise, strong speech, fast growth, and loud public action.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个表示生机的拉丁词，从强健的身体延伸到剧烈的运动、有力的言辞、旺盛的生长与声势浩大的行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a runner taking the steps two at a time.
core.cn: 核心意象：一次跨两级台阶的跑者。

branches.en: The body branch: a strong man of seventy.
branches.cn: 身体分支：七十岁仍强健的人。

branches.en: The activity branch: back to vigorous exercise.
branches.cn: 活动分支：恢复剧烈运动。

branches.en: The speech branch: a vigorous defence of the plan.
branches.cn: 言辞分支：为计划作有力辩护。

branches.en: The plant branch: growth after spring rain.
branches.cn: 植物分支：春雨后的旺盛生长。

branches.en: The group branch: a campaign against litter.
branches.cn: 群体分支：声势浩大的反垃圾运动。

intro.en: The stem vig- means to be lively; -ous and -ly build the adjective and adverb, in- adds energy to others.
intro.cn: 词干 vig- 意为有生机，-ous、-ly 构成形容词与副词，in- 表示把能量给别人。

latinIntro.en: Latin vigere produced vigor and the English family vigorous, vigorously, and invigorate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vigere 产生 vigor，以及英语中的 vigorous、vigorously、invigorate。

items.example: Vig- carries living energy.
Vigour is the state of being lively.
Vigorous means full of vigour.
They argued vigorously for an hour.
items.exampleCN: 他们激烈辩论了一小时。

items.example: Invigorate puts energy back in.
A vigil keeps watch through the night.
A feeble step next to a vigorous one.
items.exampleCN: 虚弱的步子旁边是有力的步子。

items.example: Rigorous rules are not vigorous ones.
items.exampleCN: 严格的规则不等于有力的规则。

items.example: A robust frame is a vigorous one.
items.exampleCN: 结实的体格就是强健的体格。

definition_en: a small settlement in the countryside, smaller than a town
core_image: 山谷里几十间灰瓦房，一条路从村口穿过
scene: 地图上那一点很小，但走进去有小学、有杂货铺、有坐在门口的老人。The village has one school, one shop, and two hundred people.
sceneCN: 这里 village 是「村庄」（第 1 个义项：比城镇小的乡村聚落）；句意为这个村子有一所学校、一家店、两百口人。山谷里几十间灰瓦房的画面就是这个词的意思。

derivatives.zh: 加后缀 -er 构成，义为「村民」
villager 的复数，义为「村民们」
加 -like 构成，义为「村庄般的」

senses.title: A small country settlement
senses.definition: a small group of houses in the countryside
senses.definitionCN: 乡村中一小片房屋构成的聚落
senses.example: The village has one school, one shop, and two hundred people.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子有一所学校、一家店、两百口人。
senses.why: Latin villa was a country house, and a cluster of them became a village.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 villa 是乡间宅院，几座聚在一起就成了村庄。

senses.title: The people living there
senses.definition: the inhabitants of such a place, taken together
senses.definitionCN: 住在这样一个地方的人们，作为整体看
senses.example: The whole village came out to watch the parade.
senses.exampleCN: 全村人都出来看游行。
senses.why: Once houses stand together, the word can mean the people inside them.
senses.whyCN: 房屋一旦聚在一起，这个词就可以指住在里面的人。

senses.title: A district inside a city
senses.definition: a small area of a city that feels like a country village
senses.definitionCN: 城市里像乡村村庄的一小片区域
senses.example: Greenwich Village is famous for its small streets.
senses.exampleCN: 格林尼治村以其小街巷闻名。
senses.why: City planners borrowed the warm image of the country village for an urban quarter.
senses.whyCN: 城市规划者借用了乡村村庄的温暖意象来称呼城市街区。

senses.title: A settlement in a game or story
senses.definition: a small settlement used as a setting in games and fiction
senses.definitionCN: 游戏与虚构作品中作为场景的小聚落
senses.example: Players return to the village to trade supplies.
senses.exampleCN: 玩家回到村庄交换补给。
senses.why: Any small settlement in an imagined world takes the same name.
senses.whyCN: 想象世界里的任何小聚落都沿用这个名字。

senses.title: The adjective use in names
senses.definition: used before another noun to describe something belonging to a village
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一名词前，表示属于村庄的
senses.example: Village life moves more slowly than city life.
senses.exampleCN: 乡村生活比城市生活节奏更慢。
senses.why: A settled place easily turns into a describing word.
senses.whyCN: 一个固定的地方很容易转成修饰用的词。

intro.en: Village grew from Latin villa, a country estate, through French into English.
intro.cn: village 从拉丁语 villa（乡间庄园）经法语进入英语。

items.en: Villa was a country house with land around it.
items.cn: villa 是带有周围土地的乡间宅邸。

items.en: Villaticus described what belonged to such an estate.
items.cn: villaticus 形容属于这种庄园的东西。

items.en: French village named the group of houses that grew near a villa.
items.cn: 法语 village 指在庄园附近发展起来的房屋群。

items.en: English village covered a small settlement with a church.
items.cn: 中世纪英语 village 指带教堂的小聚落。

items.en: The word later lent itself to city quarters and game settings.
items.cn: 后来这个词也被用于城市街区与游戏场景。

note.en: The first group holds the villa family, the second the nearby words for settlements.
note.cn: 第一组是 villa 词族，第二组是表示聚落的相近词。

entries.definition: a person who lives in a village
a larger settlement with shops and offices
a very small group of houses
a place where people have settled
a large and busy urban place

normalIntro.en: A villa is one house; a village is the ring of houses that gathers around it.
normalIntro.cn: villa 是一座宅子，village 是围着它聚成的房群。

normal.en: Villa plus -age gives village, as in village of houses.
normal.cn: villa 加 -age 得 village，即一片房舍。

normal.en: Add -er for villager, the person; keep the g.
normal.cn: 加 -er 得 villager（村民），注意 g 保留。

normal.en: The plural adds -s to the whole word: villages.
normal.cn: 复数在整词后加 -s：villages。

normal.en: Think small: one school, one shop, one road.
normal.cn: 往小处想：一所学校、一家店、一条路。

normal.en: Greenwich Village shows the word used inside a city.
normal.cn: Greenwich Village 展示了城市内的用法。

abstract.en: See grey roofs in a valley with one road through.
abstract.cn: 想山谷里一片灰屋顶，一条路穿过。

abstract.en: Hear a bell that the whole valley can hear.
abstract.cn: 听一口全谷都听得见的钟。

abstract.en: Picture the old men at the doorway watching the road.
abstract.cn: 想老人们坐在门口望着那条路。

examples.en: They moved from the city to a small village.
examples.cn: 他们从城市搬到了一个小村庄。

examples.en: Every villager helped rebuild the bridge.
examples.cn: 每位村民都参与了修桥。

examples.en: The village is quiet except on market day.
examples.cn: 这个村子除了集市日都很安静。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「为立志」——年轻人为了立志出山，把家乡的小村庄留在身后。

root: 拉丁语 villa（乡间庄园）→ 古法语 village → 中世纪英语 village

sensesIntro.en: One country estate grows into a cluster of houses, then into the people, then into a street of the big city.
sensesIntro.cn: 一座乡间庄园长成一片房舍，再长成住在里面的人，最后长成大城市里的一条街。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: grey roofs in a valley, one road through.
core.cn: 核心意象：山谷里的灰屋顶与一条穿村的路。

branches.en: The place branch: one school and two hundred people.
branches.cn: 地点分支：一所学校与两百个人。

branches.en: The people branch: the whole village at the parade.
branches.cn: 人物分支：全村的看游行的人。

branches.en: The city branch: small streets called a village.
branches.cn: 城市分支：被称为「村」的小街巷。

branches.en: The story branch: players trading in the village.
branches.cn: 故事分支：玩家在村里交易。

branches.en: The naming branch: village life in a report.
branches.cn: 命名分支：报道中的乡村生活。

intro.en: The stem vill- means a country estate; -age makes a collective noun, -er makes the person.
intro.cn: 词干 vill- 意为乡间庄园，-age 构成集合名词，-er 构成表人的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin villa gave French village and English village, with villager built on top.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 villa 派生法语 village 与英语 village，再由此构成 villager。

items.example: Vill- points to a house in the fields.
items.exampleCN: vill- 指向田野中的宅子。

items.example: Village is a group of villas.
A villager lives in the village.
A villagelike street in the old town.
items.exampleCN: 老城里一条像村庄的街。

items.example: Three villages share one well.
A village grows into a town.
A hamlet has no church.
They rented a villa by the sea.
items.exampleCN: 他们在海边租了一栋别墅。

items.example: A village inside a city is a neighbourhood.

definition_en: a sour liquid made from wine or cider and used in cooking, or a sour temper
core_image: 一勺深褐色的液体倒进凉菜，酸味冲上来
scene: 厨房里，她把醋倒进拌好的黄瓜，酸味立刻充满了屋子。A spoonful of vinegar gives the salad its sharp taste.
sceneCN: 这里 vinegar 是「醋」（第 1 个义项：由葡萄酒或苹果酒发酵成的酸味液体，用于调味）；句意为一勺醋让沙拉有了锐利的酸味。倒进凉菜时窜上来的酸味正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 加后缀 -y 构成，义为「酸的；尖刻的」
加后缀 -ish 构成，义为「略带酸味的」
加 -oon 构成的旧词，义为「醋虫；鞭蝎」

senses.title: A sour liquid used in cooking
senses.definition: a sour liquid produced by fermenting wine, cider, or malt, used to flavour food
senses.definitionCN: 由葡萄酒、苹果酒或麦芽发酵而成、用于调味的酸味液体
senses.example: A spoonful of vinegar gives the salad its sharp taste.
senses.exampleCN: 一勺醋让沙拉有了锐利的酸味。
senses.why: Old French vyn egre means sour wine, and sour wine is exactly what vinegar is.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 vyn egre 意为「酸酒」，而醋正是变酸的酒。

senses.title: A sour or sharp temper
senses.definition: a bitter or ill-tempered manner in speech or behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 言语或行为中尖刻、易怒的性情
senses.example: His reply was all vinegar and no help.
senses.exampleCN: 他的回答满是尖刻，毫无帮助。
senses.why: Taste words often become temper words: what stings the tongue also stings the ear.
senses.whyCN: 味道词常变成性情词：刺舌的东西也刺耳。

senses.title: In industry, a dilute acid
senses.definition: a dilute acetic acid used in cleaning, preserving, or manufacture
senses.definitionCN: 用于清洁、防腐或制造的稀醋酸
senses.example: The workshop cleans metal parts in vinegar before painting.
senses.exampleCN: 车间在喷漆前用稀醋酸清洗金属件。
senses.why: Beyond the kitchen, the same acid serves as a cheap and mild solvent.
senses.whyCN: 走出厨房，同一种酸也成了廉价温和的溶剂。

senses.title: A means of preserving food
senses.definition: a sour bath in which food is kept from spoiling
senses.definitionCN: 用来防止食物变坏的酸味浸泡液
senses.example: They keep onions in vinegar through the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用醋泡洋葱，能吃一冬天。
senses.why: The sourness that flavours food also protects it, so vinegar became a preservative.
senses.whyCN: 调味的酸同时能护住食物，于是醋成了防腐手段。

senses.title: A sharp, bitter remark
senses.definition: a comment that stings or embitters the hearer
senses.definitionCN: 刺痛或使听者不快的话
senses.example: Every suggestion was met with vinegar from the chair.
senses.exampleCN: 每个建议都被主席用尖刻的话顶了回去。
senses.why: When the temper shows itself in words, each remark is a drop of the same fluid.
senses.whyCN: 当脾气化作言语时，每一句话都是同一液体的液滴。

intro.en: Vinegar is French for sour wine: vin, wine, plus aigre, sour.
intro.cn: vinegar 就是法语的「酸酒」：vin（酒）加 aigre（酸）。

items.en: Vinum meant wine, and acer meant sharp or sour.
items.cn: vinum 意为酒，acer 意为尖的、酸的。

items.en: Vyn egre joined the two words into sour wine.
items.cn: vyn egre 把两个词合为一体，指酸酒。

items.en: English took it as vynegre in the kitchen and in medicine.
items.cn: 英语以 vynegre 借入，用于厨房和医药。

items.en: The spelling settled as vinegar in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 十七世纪拼写固定为 vinegar。

items.en: A sour temper and a sharp remark took the taste word out of the kitchen.
items.cn: 坏脾气与尖刻话把这个味觉词带出了厨房。

note.en: The first group holds the vinegar family, the second the sour tastes and sharp manners it stands beside.
note.cn: 第一组是 vinegar 词族，第二组是与酸味、尖刻并列的词。

normalIntro.en: Wine that has turned sour: that is the whole word, and the whole bottle.
normalIntro.cn: 变酸的酒——这就是整个词，也是整瓶东西。

normal.en: Vinegar hides vin, wine, at the front.
normal.cn: vinegar 前头藏着 vin，即葡萄酒。

normal.en: The -ar at the end echoes aigre, sour in French.
normal.cn: 结尾的 -ar 呼应法语 aigre（酸的）。

normal.en: Vinegar has three syllables: VIN-e-gar.
normal.cn: vinegar 有三个音节：VIN-e-gar。

normal.en: Add -y for vinegary, sour or sharp.
normal.cn: 加 -y 得 vinegary，酸的或尖刻的。

normal.en: Do not confuse vinegar with vine, the grape plant.
normal.cn: 别把 vinegar 与 vine（葡萄藤）混为一谈。

abstract.en: See dark liquid tipping from a spoon into a bowl.
abstract.cn: 想深色液体从勺里倒进碗里。

abstract.en: Smell sharp air rising from a salad.
abstract.cn: 嗅沙拉上窜起的冲鼻气。

abstract.en: Hear a voice turn sour at the end of a sentence.
abstract.cn: 听一句话的尾音突然变酸。

examples.en: Mix olive oil and vinegar for the dressing.
examples.cn: 把橄榄油和醋调成沙拉汁。

examples.en: A drop of vinegar cuts the sweetness of the sauce.
examples.cn: 一滴醋能压住酱汁的甜腻。

examples.en: There was vinegar in every word she said.
examples.cn: 她说的话里每一句都带刺。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂泥哥」——喂，泥哥，快闻闻这瓶醋，酸得呛人。

root: 拉丁语 vinum（酒）+ acer（酸的）→ 古法语 vyn egre（酸酒）→ 英语 vinegar

sensesIntro.en: Sour wine in a bottle becomes a seasoning, a preservative, an industrial acid, and at last a sour temper.
sensesIntro.cn: 瓶里的酸酒先成为调味品、防腐液、工业稀酸，最后成为酸溜溜的脾气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: dark vinegar dripping onto a salad.
core.cn: 核心意象：深色的醋滴在沙拉上。

branches.en: The kitchen branch: a spoonful on cucumber.
branches.cn: 厨房分支：黄瓜上的一勺醋。

branches.en: The temper branch: a reply all vinegar.
branches.cn: 脾气分支：满是尖刻的回答。

branches.en: The workshop branch: acid for cleaning metal.
branches.cn: 车间分支：清洗金属的稀酸。

branches.en: The jar branch: onions kept through winter.
branches.cn: 坛子分支：醋泡洋葱过冬。

branches.en: The remark branch: every suggestion stung.
branches.cn: 言语分支：每个建议都被刺回。

intro.en: Vinegar came into English whole from French; only -y and -ish were added later.
intro.cn: vinegar 从法语整体进入英语，后来只加上了 -y 与 -ish。

latinIntro.en: Its parts are Latin vinum, wine, and acer, sharp, joined in Old French before English borrowed it.
latinIntro.cn: 其成分是拉丁语 vinum（酒）与 acer（尖的），在古法语中先已拼合，英语整体借用。

items.example: Vin- in vinegar means wine.
items.exampleCN: vinegar 中的 vin- 意为酒。

items.example: -Egar echoes French aigre.
Vinegary sauce tastes sharp.
A vinegarish smell filled the room.
items.exampleCN: 屋里有一股微酸的气味。

items.example: Vine and vinegar look close but differ.
items.exampleCN: vine 与 vinegar 形近而义远。

items.example: Wine and vinegar share vinum.
items.exampleCN: wine 与 vinegar 同出 vinum。

items.example: Vinegar is a mild acid.
Write vinegar with an e after v.
items.exampleCN: vinegar 在 v 后写 e。

items.example: Sour describes what vinegar tastes of.

definition_en: to break a law, rule, or agreement, or to treat something sacred with disrespect
core_image: 一个人抬脚直接踏过围起来的白线
scene: 新闻里说，这家公司被查出违反了安全规定。The company was found to have violated safety rules.
sceneCN: 这里 violate 是「违反」（第 1 个义项：违背法律、规则或约定）；句意为这家公司被查出违反了安全规定。抬脚越过白线的那一步就是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 加后缀 -ion 构成，义为「违反；侵犯」
加后缀 -or 构成，义为「违反者；侵犯者」
同源名词，义为「暴力」

senses.title: To break a rule or law
senses.definition: to act against a law, rule, or agreement
senses.definitionCN: 做出违背法律、规则或约定的行为
senses.example: The company was found to have violated safety rules.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司被查出违反了安全规定。
senses.why: Latin violare meant to treat with force, and treating a rule with force is breaking it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 violare 意为以强力对待，用强力对待规则就是违反规则。

senses.title: To break into what belongs to another
senses.definition: to intrude on rights, privacy, or a person
senses.definitionCN: 侵入他人的权利、隐私或人身
senses.example: The reporter had violated her privacy.
senses.exampleCN: 那位记者侵犯了她的隐私。
senses.why: When force crosses a boundary that belongs to someone else, the word shifts from rules to persons.
senses.whyCN: 当强力越过属于他人的边界时，这个词就从规则转向了人。

senses.title: To treat something sacred with disrespect
senses.definition: to show contempt for a holy place or thing
senses.definitionCN: 对神圣的场所或事物表示轻慢
senses.example: Touching the altar was thought to violate the temple.
senses.exampleCN: 人们认为触碰祭坛是亵渎神庙。
senses.why: The oldest use is about holy places, where force feels most shocking.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的用法针对圣地，那里施加强力最令人震惊。

senses.title: To break a promise or agreement
senses.definition: to fail to keep what one has agreed to
senses.definitionCN: 没有履行已经同意的事情
senses.example: By selling the land he violated the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 他卖地，违反了合同。
senses.why: A contract is a rule two sides wrote, so breaking it takes the same verb.
senses.whyCN: 契约是双方一起写下的规则，破坏它用的是同一个动词。

senses.title: To disturb the peace of a place
senses.definition: to break the quiet or order of a place
senses.definitionCN: 打破某处的安静或秩序
senses.example: A siren violated the silence of the night.
senses.exampleCN: 一声警笛打破了夜的寂静。
senses.why: Quiet and order are also boundaries, and force across them is a violation.
senses.whyCN: 宁静与秩序也是边界，强力越过它们同样是侵犯。

intro.en: Violate comes from Latin violare, to treat with force or to outrage.
intro.cn: violate 来自拉丁语 violare，意为以强力对待或施暴。

items.en: Violare meant to use force on something, or to outrage it.
items.cn: violare 意为对某物施加强力，或加害凌辱。

items.en: Violentia, force, and violatio, an outrage, grew from the same stem.
items.cn: violentia（暴力）与 violatio（侵害）出自同一词干。

items.en: French violer brought the word into legal and moral talk.
items.cn: 法语 violer 把该词带入法律与道德的讨论。

items.en: English used violate for breaking holy things and sworn promises.
items.cn: 中世纪英语用 violate 指破坏神圣之物与立下的誓约。

items.en: Modern law applies it to rules, rights, contracts, and privacy.
items.cn: 现代法律将其用于规则、权利、合同与隐私。

note.en: The first group holds the violence family, the second the nearby verbs of breaking and keeping.
note.cn: 第一组是 violence 词族，第二组是表示违反与遵守的相近动词。

entries.definition: the act of breaking a rule
a person who breaks a rule
to fail to keep a rule or promise
to go beyond a legal limit
to do wrong or to hurt feelings
to do what a rule says

normalIntro.en: Violate, violence, and violent share one Latin stem: force used where it should not be.
normalIntro.cn: violate、violence、violent 共用一个拉丁词干：用在不该用的地方的强力。

normal.en: Violate is the verb, violation the act, violator the person.
normal.cn: violate 是动词，violation 是行为，violator 是人。

normal.en: That Latin stem viol- also gave violence and violent.
normal.cn: 拉丁词干 viol- 还产生了 violence 与 violent。

normal.en: You violate a rule, a right, a contract, or a quiet night.
normal.cn: 可以 violate 规则、权利、合同，也可以 violate 一个安静的夜晚。

normal.en: Notice the long i: VY-uh-late, not vee-.
normal.cn: 注意长音 i：读 VY-uh-late，不读 vee-。

normal.en: Keep the final -e before -ion: violation.
normal.cn: 加 -ion 前保留词尾 -e：violation。

abstract.en: See a foot stepping straight over a painted white line.
abstract.cn: 想一只脚直接跨过画好的白线。

abstract.en: Hear a door pushed open without a knock.
abstract.cn: 听一扇门没敲门就被推开。

abstract.en: Feel a siren cutting through a still night.
abstract.cn: 感受警笛划破寂静的夜。

examples.en: Drivers who violate the speed limit will be fined.
examples.cn: 超速的司机将被罚款。

examples.en: The new law violates the rights of small businesses.
examples.cn: 这项新法律侵犯了小企业的权利。

examples.en: He did not want to violate his promise to her.
examples.cn: 他不想违背对她的承诺。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「歪尔雷特」——把围栏特意掰歪了越过去，就是违反规定。

root: 拉丁语 violare（以强力对待；加害）→ violatio（侵害）→ 古法语 violer → 英语 violate

sensesIntro.en: A Latin verb for using force spreads from holy places to laws, to other people, to contracts, and to a quiet night.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个表示施加强力的拉丁动词，从圣地扩展到法律、他人、契约，以及一个安静的夜晚。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foot stepping over a white line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只脚跨过白线。

branches.en: The rule branch: safety rules broken by a company.
branches.cn: 规则分支：公司违反安全规定。

branches.en: The person branch: a reporter and her privacy.
branches.cn: 人身分支：记者与她的隐私。

branches.en: The temple branch: a hand on the altar.
