branches.cn: 神庙分支：触碰祭坛的手。

branches.en: The contract branch: land sold against the deal.
branches.cn: 契约分支：违约卖地。

branches.en: The quiet branch: a siren in the night.
branches.cn: 宁静分支：夜里的一声警笛。

intro.en: The Latin stem viol- carries force; -ate makes the verb, -ion and -or the noun and the person.
intro.cn: 拉丁词干 viol- 携带强力之义，-ate 构成动词，-ion、-or 构成名词与表人词。

latinIntro.en: Latin violare yielded violation, violator, and the whole violence family in English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 violare 派生英语的 violation、violator 以及整个 violence 词族。

items.example: Viol- carries the sense of force misused.
items.exampleCN: viol- 携带被误用的强力。

items.example: Violate is to act with force against.
A violation is the act itself.
A violator is the one who breaks it.
Violence is the state of using force.
items.exampleCN: violence 是使用强力的状态。

items.example: A violent act uses great force.
items.exampleCN: violent act 使用巨大强力。

items.example: Most drivers obey the limit.
The copy infringes a patent.
The remark offended the audience.

latinEntries.meaning: to treat with force, to outrage

definition_en: behaviour meant to hurt or kill people, or great force in nature or feeling
core_image: 街角围起的人群，地上散落的碎玻璃
scene: 深夜的街角围起了警戒线，地上散着碎玻璃，警察在记录现场。The city has seen a rise in violence since the summer.
sceneCN: 这里 violence 是「暴力」（第 1 个义项：意图伤害或杀害他人的行为）；句意为入夏以来这座城市的暴力事件增多了。街角围着的人群与碎玻璃正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 同源形容词，义为「暴力的；猛烈的」
加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「猛烈地」
同源动词，义为「违反；侵犯」

senses.title: Behaviour meant to hurt people
senses.definition: actions intended to injure, damage, or kill
senses.definitionCN: 意图伤害、破坏或杀害他人的行为
senses.example: The city has seen a rise in violence since the summer.
senses.exampleCN: 入夏以来这座城市的暴力事件增多了。
senses.why: From Latin violentia, the word names force pushed to the point of harm.
senses.whyCN: 这个词源自拉丁语 violentia，指被推到伤害程度的力量。

senses.title: Great force in nature
senses.definition: the destructive power of storms, earthquakes, or other natural forces
senses.definitionCN: 风暴、地震等自然力量造成的破坏力
senses.example: The violence of the storm tore roofs from houses.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴之猛把房顶都掀了下来。
senses.why: Nature uses no fists, yet a storm’s force is spoken of with the same noun.
senses.whyCN: 自然并没有拳头，但风暴的力量用的仍是这个词。

senses.title: Intensity of feeling or expression
senses.definition: extreme force in emotion, words, or action
senses.definitionCN: 情感、言辞或行为上的极端强度
senses.example: She spoke with a violence that surprised her friends.
senses.exampleCN: 她说话之激烈让朋友们吃了一惊。
senses.why: Feelings can press as hard as hands, so intensity of speech borrows the word of blows.
senses.whyCN: 情绪能像手一样用力，于是言语的激烈借用了拳头的说法。

senses.title: Unlawful force in law
senses.definition: the use of physical force against a person or property contrary to law
senses.definitionCN: 对人身或财产非法使用的物理强制
senses.example: The charge was robbery with violence.
senses.exampleCN: 罪名是暴力抢劫。
senses.why: Courts need a precise term for force that breaks the law, and violence supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 法院需要一个精确术语指违法的强制，violence 正好胜任。

senses.title: In media, images of fighting and cruelty
senses.definition: shown fighting, killing, or cruelty in films and games
senses.definitionCN: 影视与游戏中展示的打斗、杀戮或残忍
senses.example: Parents asked for less violence in the evening schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 家长要求在晚间节目里少放暴力内容。
senses.why: Once screens show the act, the noun names the content as well as the deed.
senses.whyCN: 屏幕一旦展示这种行为，这个词既指行为，也指内容。

intro.en: Violence goes back to Latin violentia, from vis, force.
intro.cn: violence 追溯至拉丁语 violentia，源自 vis（力量）。

items.en: Vis meant force or power, and violentia named the quality of using it hard.
items.cn: vis 意为力量或强力，violentia 指蛮横使用力量的性质。

items.en: Violare, to treat with force, shares the same root.
items.cn: violare（施暴、亵渎）与它同根。

items.en: French violence carried the noun into English law and letters.
items.cn: 法语 violence 把这一名词带进英语的法律与文章。

items.en: English used it first for unlawful force.
items.cn: 中世纪英语先用它指非法强制。

items.en: Storms, feelings, and screen content took the word far beyond the courtroom.
items.cn: 风暴、情感与屏幕内容把这个词带出了法庭。

note.en: The first group holds the violence family, the second the words for force, fighting, and calm.
note.cn: 第一组是 violence 词族，第二组是力量、打斗与平静的相关词。

strength used on a person or thing

normalIntro.en: The root vis, force, fills the word: violence is force taken too far.
normalIntro.cn: 词根 vis（力量）贯穿全词：暴力就是把力量用过了头。

normal.en: Violet and violence look alike; only the ending differs.
normal.cn: violet 与 violence 形近，只差词尾。

normal.en: Violence ends in -ence, like patience.
normal.cn: violence 以 -ence 结尾，如同 patience。

normal.en: The adjective drops -nce for -nt: violent.
normal.cn: 形容词把 -nce 换成 -nt：violent。

normal.en: Resort to violence is a fixed phrase for turning to force.
normal.cn: 诉诸暴力常说 resort to violence。

normal.en: The stress falls on the first syllable: VI-o-lence.
normal.cn: 重音在第一音节：VI-o-lence。

abstract.en: See broken glass on a corner at night.
abstract.cn: 想夜里街角的碎玻璃。

abstract.en: Hear a window shake as the storm hits.
abstract.cn: 听风暴来时的窗玻璃作响。

abstract.en: Picture a hand clenched over a table.
abstract.cn: 想桌子上一只攥紧的手。

examples.en: The report calls for an end to violence in the home.
examples.cn: 这份报告呼吁终止家庭暴力。

examples.en: No cause justifies the use of violence.
examples.cn: 任何理由都不能为使用暴力开脱。

examples.en: The violence of the waves kept the boats in port.
examples.cn: 浪势太猛，船都留在了港里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「外来冷死」——外来的人被打得冷死在街头，这桩暴力令人心惊。

root: 拉丁语 vis（力量）→ violentia（强暴）→ 古法语 violence → 英语 violence

sensesIntro.en: Force used against people becomes the force of storms, of speech, of law, and of what screens show.
sensesIntro.cn: 用在人身上的力量，进而变成风暴之力、言语之力、法律上的强制与屏幕上的内容。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a police line around broken glass at night.
core.cn: 核心意象：夜里警戒线围住的碎玻璃。

branches.en: The street branch: more attacks since summer.
branches.cn: 街头分支：入夏后袭击增多。

branches.en: The storm branch: roofs torn away.
branches.cn: 风暴分支：房顶被掀掉。

branches.en: The voice branch: a tone that startles friends.
branches.cn: 语气分支：让朋友吃惊的激烈语调。

branches.en: The court branch: a charge of robbery with force.
branches.cn: 法庭分支：暴力抢劫的罪名。

branches.en: The screen branch: parents ask for less of it.
branches.cn: 屏幕分支：家长要求少放暴力。

intro.en: The root viol-, from Latin vis, force, builds violence, violent, violate, and violation.
intro.cn: 词根 viol- 源自拉丁语 vis（力量），构成 violence、violent、violate、violation。

latinIntro.en: Latin vis, force, gives violentia; the -ence ending marks an abstract noun, as in patience.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vis（力量）派生 violentia；-ence 词尾标记抽象名词，如同 patience。

items.example: Viol- carries the sense of force.
Violence names the state of using force.
items.exampleCN: violence 指使用力量的状态。

items.example: Violent means acting with force.
The door shut violently.
Violate means to break with force.
A violation of the rule was reported.
items.exampleCN: 有人举报了违反规则之事。

items.example: Force is the plain word behind vis.
items.exampleCN: force 是 vis 背后的平实说法。

items.example: Peace is what violence destroys.
items.exampleCN: 和平正是暴力所破坏的。

items.example: Violet shares the start but not the root.
items.exampleCN: violet 与它开头相同而词根不同。

definition_en: using or involving force meant to hurt, or happening with great force
core_image: 被人一把推开的门，撞在墙上反弹回来
scene: 电影里两个人争执起来，其中一个一把把桌子掀翻，杯子全摔在地上。The argument turned violent before anyone could stop it.
sceneCN: 这里 violent 是「暴力的」（第 1 个义项：涉及意在伤害他人的武力）；句意为还没人来得及阻止，争吵就演变成暴力冲突。被掀翻的桌子与砸碎的杯子正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 去后缀 -ent 构成的名词，义为「暴力」
加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「猛烈地」
加前缀 non- 构成，义为「非暴力的」

senses.title: Using force to hurt people
senses.definition: using physical force intended to injure or kill
senses.definitionCN: 使用意在伤害或杀害他人的体力
senses.example: The argument turned violent before anyone could stop it.
senses.exampleCN: 还没人来得及阻止，争吵就演变成了暴力冲突。
senses.why: A violent act is force aimed at a body, and the sentence usually shows a body receiving it.
senses.whyCN: 暴力行为是针对人体施加的力量，句子里往往能看到承受的那具身体。

senses.title: Happening with great natural force
senses.definition: of weather or natural events, striking with great power
senses.definitionCN: 天气或自然现象以巨大力量袭来
senses.example: A violent storm closed the harbour for two days.
senses.exampleCN: 一场猛烈的风暴让港口停摆两天。
senses.why: Nature strikes with the same force as a fist, so the adjective crosses over.
senses.whyCN: 自然的力量与拳头一样，形容词因此跨了过来。

senses.title: Extremely strong in feeling
senses.definition: of feelings, reactions, or changes, very strong and sudden
senses.definitionCN: 指情感、反应或变化非常强烈而突然
senses.example: He had a violent dislike of being interrupted.
senses.exampleCN: 他极其厌恶被人打断。
senses.why: A feeling that arrives with force takes the adjective of force, even without any blow.
senses.whyCN: 猛然涌来的情绪也用了表示力量的那个形容词，即便没有任何一击。

senses.title: In law, involving force against a person
senses.definition: of a crime, committed with force against a person
senses.definitionCN: 指犯罪时对人使用了强制
senses.example: He was charged with violent robbery.
senses.exampleCN: 他被控暴力抢劫。
senses.why: Law separates crimes with force from those without, and the adjective does that work.
senses.whyCN: 法律把带强制的犯罪与不带强制的分开，这个形容词正承担这一区分。

senses.title: In colour or light, very intense
senses.definition: of colour, extremely bright and harsh to the eye
senses.definitionCN: 指颜色极其鲜明、刺眼
senses.example: A violent orange covered the whole wall.
senses.exampleCN: 整面墙刷成了刺眼的橘色。
senses.why: Strong colour hits the eye the way a blow hits the body, so the sense extends.
senses.whyCN: 强烈的颜色冲击眼睛，如同打击冲击身体，词义由此延伸。

intro.en: Violent comes from Latin violentia, the quality of force.
intro.cn: violent 来自拉丁语 violentia，指力量的性质。

items.en: Vis was force, and violentus described one full of it.
items.cn: vis 是力量，violentus 形容充满力量的人。

items.en: The adjective came before the English noun, both from the same stem.
items.cn: 形容词先于英语名词出现，二者同出一词干。

items.en: French violent passed the adjective into English.
items.cn: 法语 violent 把形容词传入英语。

items.en: English used it for blows, storms, and heated speech.
items.cn: 中世纪英语用它指打击、风暴与激烈的言辞。

items.en: Colour and reaction senses joined in later centuries.
items.cn: 色彩与反应等义项在之后的世纪加入。

note.en: The first group holds the violent family, the second the adjectives for force, rage, and calm.
note.cn: 第一组是 violent 词族，第二组是力量、愤怒与平静的形容词。

normalIntro.en: The ending -ent marks the adjective; the stem marks the force.
normalIntro.cn: 词尾 -ent 标记形容词，词干标记力量。

normal.en: Drop -ent and add -ence for the noun violence.
normal.cn: 去掉 -ent 加 -ence 得名词 violence。

normal.en: Add -ly for violently, with force in the manner.
normal.cn: 加 -ly 得 violently，表示方式猛烈。

normal.en: Nonviolent puts non- in front to deny the force.
normal.cn: nonviolent 前置 non- 以否定力量。

normal.en: Compare with more violent, not violenter.
normal.cn: 比较级用 more violent，不用 violenter。

normal.en: The second syllable is weak: VI-o-lent.
normal.cn: 第二音节弱读：VI-o-lent。

abstract.en: See a table thrown over in a quarrel.
abstract.cn: 想争吵中桌子被掀翻。

abstract.en: Hear a door slam and bounce off the wall.
abstract.cn: 听门被摔上又弹回墙上。

abstract.en: Picture an orange too bright to look at.
abstract.cn: 想一片亮得刺眼的橘色。

examples.en: The crowd grew violent after the refused request.
examples.cn: 请求被拒之后人群动起手来。

examples.en: A violent wind tore the sails in minutes.
examples.cn: 一阵狂风几分钟就把帆撕破了。

examples.en: Her violent reaction showed how much the news hurt.
examples.cn: 她激烈的反应说明这消息伤她多深。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「外冷特」——外面冷得特厉害，风刮得跟砸门一样猛。

root: 拉丁语 vis（力量）→ violentus（充满力量的）→ 古法语 violent → 英语 violent

sensesIntro.en: Force aimed at people, storms, feelings, crimes, and even paint share one adjective.
sensesIntro.cn: 针对人的力量、风暴、情绪、罪名，甚至油漆，共用同一个形容词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door flung so hard it bounces off the wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：门被摔得撞墙反弹。

branches.en: The quarrel branch: a table thrown over.
branches.cn: 争执分支：桌子被掀翻。

branches.en: The harbour branch: a storm stopping the boats.
branches.cn: 港口分支：风暴让船停航。

branches.en: The temper branch: hatred of interruption.
branches.cn: 性情分支：对被打算的厌恶。

branches.en: The charge branch: robbery with force.
branches.cn: 控告分支：暴力抢劫。

branches.en: The paint branch: an orange too bright for the eye.
branches.cn: 油漆分支：刺眼的橘色。

intro.en: Violent shares the stem viol- with violence and violate; -ent makes it an adjective.
intro.cn: violent 与 violence、violate 共用词干 viol-，-ent 使其成为形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin violentus described what is full of vis, force; the ending -ent means having that quality.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 violentus 形容充满 vis（力量）之物，-ent 意为具有该性质。

items.example: Viol- is the force in violent.
items.exampleCN: viol- 是 violent 中的力量。

items.example: Violent means full of force.
Violence names the state.
The wind blew violently.
Nonviolent protest keeps to peace.
Vis is the bare Latin noun.
items.exampleCN: vis 是裸露的拉丁名词。

items.example: Fierce is close but less legal.
items.exampleCN: fierce 相近但少了法律色彩。

items.example: Gentle hands replace violent ones.
items.exampleCN: 温和的手取代粗暴的手。

definition_en: in a way that uses great force, or that involves hurting people
core_image: 一扇窗在风里剧烈撞动，玻璃嗡嗡作响
scene: 夜里起了风，旧窗框被吹得来回撞动，玻璃嗡嗡直响，她只好起身去关。The shutters banged violently against the wall all night.
sceneCN: 这里 violently 是「猛烈地」（第 1 个义项：以极大的力量进行）；句意为百叶窗整夜猛烈地拍打墙面。风里撞动的窗与嗡嗡的玻璃正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 去后缀 -ly 构成的形容词，义为「暴力的；猛烈的」
同源名词，义为「暴力」
加前缀 non- 构成，义为「非暴力地」

senses.title: With great physical force
senses.definition: with a very strong physical movement or impact
senses.definitionCN: 以极强的人体动作或冲击力
senses.example: The shutters banged violently against the wall all night.
senses.exampleCN: 百叶窗整夜猛烈地拍打墙面。
senses.why: The adverb answers how a thing moves, and here the answer is with everything it has.
senses.whyCN: 副词回答「怎么动」，这里的回答是「用尽全身之力」。

senses.title: In a way that hurts people
senses.definition: in a manner that involves attacking or harming someone
senses.definitionCN: 以攻击或伤害他人的方式进行
senses.example: The crowd was violently broken up by police.
senses.exampleCN: 人群被警察以暴力方式驱散。
senses.why: The adjective means force against people; the adverb says that the action was done that way.
senses.whyCN: 形容词指针对人的力量；副词说明这一动作正是那样完成的。

senses.title: Extremely, in a sudden and ungoverned way
senses.definition: to an extreme and sudden degree, of changes or reactions
senses.definitionCN: 指变化或反应极端而突然
senses.example: He reacted violently to the medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 他对这种药反应剧烈。
senses.why: A body or a system can lurch as if struck, and the adverb marks the lurch.
senses.whyCN: 身体或系统可能像被击中般剧变，副词标记的正是这次剧变。

senses.title: With strong opposition in speech
senses.definition: in a very strong and hostile manner of speaking or objecting
senses.definitionCN: 以非常强烈且对立的言辞表示
senses.example: The plan was violently opposed in the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 会上这个计划遭到激烈反对。
senses.why: Words can be thrown as hard as stones, so the adverb slips into argument.
senses.whyCN: 话可以像石头一样掷出，副词于是进入了争论的场景。

senses.title: Of colour or emotion, very intensely
senses.definition: in an intensity that strikes the senses or the feelings hard
senses.definitionCN: 指以冲击感官或情感的方式表现出来
senses.example: The sky was violently red at sunset.
senses.exampleCN: 日落时天空红得刺眼。
senses.why: Anything that hits the eye or heart too hard takes this adverb of force.
senses.whyCN: 凡是过猛地冲击眼睛或心的东西，都用这个表示力量的副词。

intro.en: Violently is the adjective violent plus the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: violently 是形容词 violent 加副词词尾 -ly。

items.en: Vis meant force, and violentus described what is full of it.
items.cn: vis 意为力量，violentus 形容充满力量之物。

items.en: French violent brought the adjective into English.
items.cn: 法语 violent 把形容词带入英语。

items.en: The suffix -ly turned adjectives into adverbs ruling verbs.
items.cn: 词尾 -ly 把形容词变为修饰动词的副词。

items.en: Violently settled into the adverb of storms, blows, and reactions.
items.cn: violently 固定为风暴、打击与反应的副词。

items.en: It extends to speech and colour, wherever intensity is extreme.
items.cn: 它延伸到言辞与色彩，凡强度极端之处皆可用。

note.en: The first group holds the violent family, the second the adverbs of force and calm.
note.cn: 第一组是 violent 词族，第二组是力量与平静的副词。

normalIntro.en: Take the adjective, add -ly, and the manner becomes an adverb of force.
normalIntro.cn: 形容词加 -ly，方式便成了表示力量的副词。

normal.en: Violent plus -ly gives violently, with nothing dropped.
normal.cn: violent 加 -ly 即 violently，中间不省字母。

normal.en: Shake violently is a common pairing in reports.
normal.cn: 新闻报道里 shake violently 常连用。

normal.en: It ends in -ly, but does not mean like a violent person only.
normal.cn: 它虽以 -ly 结尾，却不只表示「像暴徒那样」。

normal.en: Use more violently for comparison.
normal.cn: 比较时用 more violently。

normal.en: The four syllables are light in the middle: VI-o-lent-ly.
normal.cn: 四个音节，中间轻读：VI-o-lent-ly。

abstract.en: See a shutter hammering the wall in a gale.
abstract.cn: 想大风里百叶窗不停拍墙。

abstract.en: Feel an engine judder under a hand.
abstract.cn: 感受手下发动机的抖动。

abstract.en: Picture a red sky that is hard to look at.
abstract.cn: 想一片红得让人不能直视的天空。

examples.en: The plane shook violently as it passed the storm.
examples.cn: 飞机穿越大风区时剧烈颠簸。

examples.en: She was violently sick after the boat trip.
examples.cn: 坐完船她吐得很厉害。

examples.en: The proposal was violently attacked by two members.
examples.cn: 这项提议遭到两位委员的激烈抨击。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「歪了伦特」——招牌被风吹歪了，伦特家的大门被拍得咣咣响。

root: 拉丁语 vis（力量）→ violentus → 古法语 violent → 英语 violent + -ly → violently

sensesIntro.en: How things move, strike, react, argue, and glow: one adverb answers all of them with force.
sensesIntro.cn: 东西怎么动、怎么撞、怎么反应、怎么争论、怎么发光：一个副词一律答以「猛烈」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a window slamming in the wind.
core.cn: 核心意象：风中来回撞击的窗。

branches.en: The shutter branch: banging against the wall.
branches.cn: 百叶窗分支：不停拍墙。

branches.en: The crowd branch: police breaking it up by force.
branches.cn: 人群分支：警察以暴力驱散。

branches.en: The medicine branch: the body lurching in reaction.
branches.cn: 药物分支：身体的剧烈反应。

branches.en: The meeting branch: a plan opposed with heat.
branches.cn: 会议分支：计划遭激烈反对。

branches.en: The sunset branch: a sky too red to bear.
branches.cn: 落日分支：红得刺眼的天空。

intro.en: The stem viol- means force; -ent and -ly turn it first into an adjective, then an adverb.
intro.cn: 词干 viol- 意为力量，-ent 与 -ly 依次把它变为形容词与副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vis, force, gives violentus; English adds -ly to make the manner adverb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vis（力量）派生 violentus，英语再加 -ly 构成方式副词。

items.example: Viol- is the force in the word.
Violent means full of force.
Violently tells how the door moved.
They protested nonviolently.
items.exampleCN: 他们以非暴力方式抗议。

items.example: Vis is the root noun.
Violentus is the Latin source.
Fiercely suggests an animal heat.
items.exampleCN: fiercely 带有野兽般的火热。

items.example: Gently closes what violently opened.
items.exampleCN: 轻轻地关上被猛烈打开的门。

definition_zh: 紫罗兰；紫罗兰色；紫色的
definition_en: a small spring flower with purple petals, or the bluish-purple colour of it
core_image: 墙根下几朵小小的紫花，藏在叶子中间
scene: 早春的花坛边，几朵紫花从枯叶里探出来，矮矮的，不显眼。A few violets had opened under the hedge before the last frost.
sceneCN: 这里 violet 是「紫罗兰」（第 1 个义项：花瓣呈紫蓝色的小型春季花卉）；句意为末次霜降前，树篱下已有几朵紫罗兰开了。花坛边藏在叶间的小紫花正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 加后缀 -aceous 构成，义为「紫罗兰色的」
加前缀 ultra- 构成，义为「紫外的」
加后缀 -like 构成，义为「似紫罗兰的」

senses.title: A small spring flower of the violet family
senses.definition: a low plant with purple or bluish flowers that blooms in spring
senses.definitionCN: 一种春天开紫蓝色花的矮小植物
senses.example: A few violets had opened under the hedge before the last frost.
senses.exampleCN: 末次霜降前，树篱下已有几朵紫罗兰开了。
senses.why: Latin viola named the flower long before any colour took its name.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 viola 早在任何颜色以它命名之前就指这种花。

senses.title: The bluish-purple colour
senses.definition: a colour between blue and purple, like the petal of the flower
senses.definitionCN: 介于蓝与紫之间的颜色，如花瓣之色
senses.example: The evening sky turned a deep violet.
senses.exampleCN: 傍晚的天空变成深紫罗兰色。
senses.why: Flowers are the easiest colour samples, so the bloom lent its name to a hue.
senses.whyCN: 花是最方便的颜色样本，于是花朵把名字借给了这一色调。

senses.title: As an adjective, of that colour
senses.definition: having the colour of the violet flower
senses.definitionCN: 具有紫罗兰花的颜色
senses.example: She wore a violet ribbon in her hair.
senses.exampleCN: 她头发上系着一条紫色缎带。
senses.why: Once the noun names a colour, it can stand before another noun as a description.
senses.whyCN: 名词一旦指某种颜色，就能放在另一名词前作修饰。

senses.title: Part of the visible spectrum near ultraviolet
senses.definition: the part of the spectrum just beyond blue, next to ultraviolet
senses.definitionCN: 光谱中紧接蓝色、靠近紫外线的一端
senses.example: Violet is the last colour the eye can see before darkness.
senses.exampleCN: 紫色是眼睛在进入黑暗前能看见的最后一种颜色。
senses.why: Physics needed a name for the short-wave end, and the deepest flower colour supplied it.
senses.whyCN: 物理学需要为短波一端命名，而最深的花色刚好胜任。

senses.title: In chemistry, a violet colour as a test result
senses.definition: the purple colour that signals a particular reaction
senses.definitionCN: 表示某一特定反应的紫色现象
senses.example: The liquid turned violet when the iodine was added.
senses.exampleCN: 加入碘之后液体变成了紫色。
senses.why: Laboratory notes borrow colour words, because a change of hue is the result.
senses.whyCN: 实验室记录借用颜色词，因为色调变化本身就是结果。

intro.en: Violet comes from Latin viola, the flower, through French.
intro.cn: violet 经法语来自拉丁语 viola（这种花）。

items.en: Viola was the Latin name for the violet and similar plants.
items.cn: viola 是拉丁语中紫罗兰及其近缘植物的名称。

items.en: Violarium named a bed of such flowers.
items.cn: violarium 指种着这类花的花圃。

items.en: French violete named the little flower with a diminutive ending.
items.cn: 法语 violete 以指小词尾命名这种小花。

items.en: English took violette, later shortened to violet.
items.cn: 英语借入 violette，后简作 violet。

items.en: The colour sense grew from the flower and reached physics.
items.cn: 颜色义由花而来，最终进入物理学。

note.en: The first group holds the violet family, the second the colours and flowers it stands among.
note.cn: 第一组是 violet 词族，第二组是与其并列的颜色与花卉词。

entries.definition: a pale purple, or its bush
a garden flower of the violet family

normalIntro.en: A small flower first, a colour second: the name travels from the garden to the paint pot.
normalIntro.cn: 先是小花，才是颜色：名字从花园走进了颜料盒。

normal.en: Violet and violin both start with vio-, but share no root.
normal.cn: violet 与 violin 都以 vio- 开头，却不同源。

normal.en: Ultraviolet puts ultra- before the colour.
normal.cn: ultraviolet 在颜色词前加 ultra-。

normal.en: The plural is violets, plainly adding s.
normal.cn: 复数 violets，直接加 s。

normal.en: Violet is two syllables with the stress on the first.
normal.cn: violet 两个音节，重音在第一个。

normal.en: The Latin plant name viola also gives the instrument’s name.
normal.cn: 拉丁植物名 viola 也给出了乐器名。

abstract.en: See a few small purple flowers under a hedge.
abstract.cn: 想树篱下几朵小小的紫花。

abstract.en: Picture the sky going deep purple after sunset.
abstract.cn: 想日落后天色转成深紫。

abstract.en: Hear a ribbon rustle in a child’s hair.
abstract.cn: 听孩子发间缎带的窸窣声。

examples.en: She picked a violet for her buttonhole.
examples.cn: 她摘了一朵紫罗兰别在扣眼上。

examples.en: The dye gave the cloth a soft violet shade.
examples.cn: 这染料把布染成了柔和的紫色。

examples.en: Too much violet in the photo makes it look cold.
examples.cn: 照片里紫色过多显得冷。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂来特」——喂，快来看这朵特紫的小花，就是紫罗兰。

root: 拉丁语 viola（紫罗兰属植物）→ 古法语 violete → 英语 violet

sensesIntro.en: One flower name becomes a colour, an adjective, a band of the spectrum, and a sign in the lab.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个花名变成了颜色、形容词、光谱的一端与实验室里的现象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: small purple flowers under a hedge.
core.cn: 核心意象：树篱下的小紫花。

branches.en: The garden branch: flowers opening before the frost.
branches.cn: 花园分支：霜前绽开的花。

branches.en: The sky branch: deep violet after sunset.
branches.cn: 天空分支：日落后的深紫。

branches.en: The ribbon branch: a violet band in the hair.
branches.cn: 缎带分支：发间的紫色带子。

branches.en: The spectrum branch: the last colour before dark.
branches.cn: 光谱分支：黑暗之前的最后一色。

branches.en: The test-tube branch: liquid turning violet.
branches.cn: 试管分支：液体变紫。

intro.en: The root viol- names the flower and its colour; -et is a French diminutive ending.
intro.cn: 词根 viol- 指这种花与其色，-et 是法语指小词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin viola gives the plant; French added the diminutive -ete, English kept the shortened -et.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 viola 给出植物名，法语加指小词尾 -ete，英语保留了缩短的 -et。

items.example: Viol- is the plant in violet.
items.exampleCN: viol- 是 violet 中的那种植物。

items.example: The ending once meant a little flower.
Violets grew along the path.
Ultraviolet lies beyond violet.
Violaceous means violet coloured.
A violet-like scent filled the room.
items.exampleCN: 屋里充满似紫罗兰的香气。

items.meaning: the plant genus, and an instrument
items.example: Viola names the plant family.
Purple covers more shades than violet.
items.exampleCN: purple 涵盖的色调比 violet 更广。

definition_en: a small wooden instrument with four strings, played with a bow
core_image: 肩上架着一把琴，琴弓停在弦上的一瞬
scene: 排练厅里，首席把琴架上肩，弓子一落，整个乐队都跟着定下音来。She tuned her violin before the orchestra began to play.
sceneCN: 这里 violin 是「小提琴」（第 1 个义项：四弦、以弓拉奏的小型木制乐器）；句意为乐团开演前她给小提琴调了音。肩上架琴、弓停在弦上的那一瞬正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 加后缀 -ist 构成，义为「小提琴手」
同族名词，义为「中提琴」
加后缀 -istic 构成，义为「小提琴演奏风格的」

senses.title: The four-stringed instrument played with a bow
senses.definition: a small bowed string instrument with four strings and a high voice
senses.definitionCN: 四弦、以弓拉奏、音色高亢的小型弦乐器
senses.example: She tuned her violin before the orchestra began to play.
senses.exampleCN: 乐团开演前她给小提琴调了音。
senses.why: Italian violino means a small viola, and smallness is exactly what makes it the leading voice.
senses.whyCN: 意大利语 violino 意为「小维奥尔」，而正是它的小巧使它成为主导声部。

senses.title: The violin section of an orchestra
senses.definition: the group of players who play violins in an orchestra
senses.definitionCN: 乐团中演奏小提琴的一组人
senses.example: The violins came in a beat early.
senses.exampleCN: 小提琴声部早进了一拍。
senses.why: Orchestras name whole sections after the instrument, so violins can mean the players.
senses.whyCN: 乐团以乐器命名整个声部，于是 violins 也可指演奏的人。

senses.title: The violin part of a score
senses.definition: the line of music written for the instrument in a work
senses.definitionCN: 乐曲中写给这一乐器的谱线
senses.example: The violin enters alone in the second movement.
senses.exampleCN: 第二乐章里小提琴独自进入。
senses.why: A score labels its lines by instrument, so the word also marks a place in the page.
senses.whyCN: 乐谱以乐器标注谱线，因此这个词也指页面上的那一行。

senses.title: The craft and trade of making violins
senses.definition: the instrument regarded as an object of fine craft
senses.definitionCN: 作为精细工艺品的这类乐器
senses.example: That violin was made in Cremona three centuries ago.
senses.exampleCN: 那把琴是三百年前在克雷莫纳制作的。
senses.why: Some instruments outlive players and become objects of craft, and the word names them so.
senses.whyCN: 有些乐器比演奏者更长寿，成为工艺对象，这个词就用来称呼它们。

senses.title: In idiom, the second place after the leader
senses.definition: the position of playing second to another, in the phrase second fiddle or second violin
senses.definitionCN: 在「第二小提琴」一类说法中，指居于他人之后的位置
senses.example: He was happy to play second violin in the project.
senses.exampleCN: 他乐意在这个项目里打下手。
senses.why: Since the section has a leader, playing second violin became a picture of a lesser role.
senses.whyCN: 既然声部有首席，拉第二小提琴便成了次要角色的写照。

intro.en: Violin is Italian violino, a small viola, from Medieval Latin vitula, a stringed instrument.
intro.cn: violin 是意大利语 violino（小维奥尔），来自中世纪拉丁语 vitula（弦乐器）。

items.en: Vitula named a stringed instrument in late Latin.
items.cn: 后期的拉丁语中，vitula 指一种弦乐器。

items.en: The word passed into the Romance languages as viola, a bowed instrument.
items.cn: 该词进入罗曼语族作 viola，指弓弦乐器。

items.en: Italian added the diminutive -ino, giving violino, the small one.
items.cn: 意大利语加指小词尾 -ino，得 violino，即小的那种。

items.en: English borrowed violin in the seventeenth century with the new craft.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪随这门新工艺借入 violin。

items.en: The word covered both the instrument and its players in an orchestra.
items.cn: 这个词既指乐器，也指乐团里的演奏者。

note.en: The first group holds the violin family, the second the other bowed strings.
note.cn: 第一组是 violin 词族，第二组是其他弓弦乐器。

entries.definition: more than one instrument or the section
the same instrument in folk music
the stick with hair that draws the sound

normalIntro.en: A small viola in Italian: the ending made the instrument and the instrument made the word.
normalIntro.cn: 意大利语里的「小维奥尔」：词尾造出乐器，乐器也定下这个词。

normal.en: Violin is Italian for a small viola.
normal.cn: violin 就是意大利语里的「小维奥尔」。

normal.en: Add -ist for violinist, the player.
normal.cn: 加 -ist 得 violinist，演奏者。

normal.en: The stress falls at the end: vi-o-LIN.
normal.cn: 重音在末尾：vi-o-LIN。

normal.en: Play the violin takes the definite article.
normal.cn: 乐器前要加定冠词：play the violin。

normal.en: Violet and violin share letters, not history.
normal.cn: violet 与 violin 只是字母相近，并无同源关系。

abstract.en: See a bow hovering one second above the strings.
abstract.cn: 想弓子在弦上方悬停一瞬。

abstract.en: Hear a single high note cut through an orchestra.
abstract.cn: 听一个高音穿透全团。

abstract.en: Picture a wooden body glowing under stage light.
abstract.cn: 想木琴身在灯光下发亮。

examples.en: He has played the violin since he was six.
examples.cn: 他六岁就开始拉小提琴。

examples.en: The violins carried the melody in the finale.
examples.cn: 终曲里旋律由小提琴声部承担。

examples.en: She teaches violin at the music school.
examples.cn: 她在音乐学校教小提琴。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「外俄林」——外面俄式林子里，有人拉起了小提琴。

root: 拉丁语 vitula（弦乐器）→ 中世纪拉丁语 viola → 意大利语 violino（小维奥尔）→ 英语 violin

sensesIntro.en: One instrument name stretches to cover its players, its lines in a score, its craft, and a modest place in a project.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个乐器名延伸去指演奏者、乐谱上的声部、制琴工艺，以及项目里的次要位置。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bow resting still above four strings.
core.cn: 核心意象：弓子静停在四根弦上方。

branches.en: The rehearsal branch: tuning before the concert.
branches.cn: 排练分支：演出前调音。

branches.en: The section branch: the violins entering early.
branches.cn: 声部分支：小提琴声部早进一拍。

branches.en: The score branch: the violin alone in the slow movement.
branches.cn: 乐谱分支：慢乐章里小提琴独奏。

branches.en: The workshop branch: a Cremona violin of great age.
branches.cn: 工坊分支：克雷莫纳的老琴。

branches.en: The idiom branch: playing second in a project.
branches.cn: 习语分支：在项目里拉第二琴。

intro.en: The stem viol- plus the Italian diminutive -in makes violin; -ist names the player.
intro.cn: 词干 viol- 加意大利语指小词尾 -in 构成 violin，-ist 指演奏者。

latinIntro.en: Latin vitula became viola in the Romance languages; Italian shrank it with -ino, and English kept the form.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vitula 在罗曼语族成为 viola，意大利语以 -ino 缩小，英语沿用了这一形式。

items.example: Viol- names the string family.
The -in once meant a small viola.
A violinist plays the instrument.
Violinistic writing suits the high strings.
items.exampleCN: 小提琴化的写法适合高音弦。

items.example: The violins were retuned.
items.exampleCN: 小提琴声部重新调了音。

items.example: A viola lies between violin and cello.
items.exampleCN: 中提琴介于小提琴与大提琴之间。

items.example: Viols came before violins.
Fiddle is the same thing in folk music.
items.exampleCN: fiddle 是民间音乐里的同一件乐器。

definition_zh: 实际的；事实上的；（计算机）虚拟的
definition_en: almost or in effect so, though not formally, and, in computing, created by software rather than existing physically
core_image: 戴上头显后，房间里凭空出现一张桌子
scene: 老师宣布这学期有几次课在线上进行，用的是一个虚拟教室。The class met in a virtual classroom twice a week.
sceneCN: 这里 virtual 是「虚拟的」（第 3 个义项：由软件生成而非实物存在的）；句意为这门课每周两次在虚拟教室上课。戴上头显后凭空出现的桌子就是这个词的画面。

pos.zh: 实际的；事实上的；虚拟的

derivatives.zh: 加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「几乎；实际上」
复合名词，义为「虚拟现实」
加后缀 -ity 构成，义为「虚拟性」

senses.title: In effect, though not in name
senses.definition: true in practice even if not officially so
senses.definitionCN: 事实上成立，但未获正式名义的
senses.example: The few shareholders hold a virtual monopoly.
senses.exampleCN: 少数股东握有近乎垄断的地位。
senses.why: Medieval Latin virtualis meant having a power or effect, and an effect can be real without a name.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪拉丁语 virtualis 意为具有效力，而效力可以真实却无名分。

senses.title: Almost, very nearly
senses.definition: so close to being so that the difference hardly matters
senses.definitionCN: 已经接近到差别几乎无关紧要
senses.example: There was a virtual absence of evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 几乎完全没有证据。
senses.why: If the effect is already there, the word can measure how near a thing is to being complete.
senses.whyCN: 效力既已存在，这个词便可以用来衡量事物接近完整的程度。

senses.title: Created by computer rather than real
senses.definition: made to exist by software, as a place or object on a screen
senses.definitionCN: 由软件生成、存在于屏幕中的场所或事物
senses.example: The class met in a virtual classroom twice a week.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课每周两次在虚拟教室上课。
senses.why: Software produces effects that feel real, which is exactly the old sense of the word in a new machine.
senses.whyCN: 软件产生了感觉真实的效力，正是这个词旧义在新机器中的化身。

senses.title: Existing in power but not in act
senses.titleCN: 潜在的；实质上的（哲学术语）
senses.definition: existing as a capacity that may become actual
senses.definitionCN: 作为一种尚未实现的能力而存在
senses.example: Scholastic writers spoke of the oak as virtual in the acorn.
senses.exampleCN: 经院学者说橡树潜在于橡子之中。
senses.why: The oldest philosophical use is about powers folded inside a thing.
senses.whyCN: 最早的哲学用法说的就是存在于事物内部的力量。

senses.title: Supported by software instead of hardware
senses.definition: of memory or storage, provided by software rather than by added hardware
senses.definitionCN: 内存或存储由软件提供而非增加硬件
senses.example: Virtual memory lets the computer run large programs.
senses.exampleCN: 虚拟内存让电脑能运行大型程序。
senses.why: A machine that has no extra chip can still behave as if it did.
senses.whyCN: 没有加芯片的机器也能表现得像加了芯片。

intro.en: Virtual descends from Latin virtus, power or worth, and first meant having that power in effect.
intro.cn: virtual 源自拉丁语 virtus（力量、价值），最初意为「在效力上具有该力量」。

items.en: Virtus meant strength, worth, and the power to act.
items.cn: virtus 意为力量、价值与行动的能力。

items.en: Virtualis described something that holds a power in effect.
items.cn: virtualis 形容在效力上持有某种力量的事物。

items.en: English virtual first meant effective, of a medicine or a power.
items.cn: 中世纪英语 virtual 最初指有效的，用于药物或力量。

items.en: By the seventeenth century it meant in effect but not in name.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，它表示「事实上如此但名义上不是」。

items.en: Computing added the sense of made by software in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 二十世纪计算机领域又增添了「由软件生成」的含义。

note.en: The first group holds the virtue family, the second the words for real and nearly.
note.cn: 第一组是 virtue 词族，第二组是表示真实与几乎的词。

entries.definition: copied to look or feel real

normalIntro.en: Virtual and virtue share a root about power; what has the power of a thing counts as that thing.
normalIntro.cn: virtual 与 virtue 共有表示「力量」的词根；具有某物效力者便算作该物。

normal.en: Virtue, virtuous, and virtual all come from Latin virtus, power.
normal.cn: virtue、virtuous、virtual 都来自拉丁语 virtus（力量）。

normal.en: Virtual reality is real in effect but not in substance.
normal.cn: 虚拟现实在效力上真实，在实体上不真实。

normal.en: The adverb is simply virtual plus -ly: virtually.
normal.cn: 副词就是 virtual 加 -ly：virtually。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with virtual memory only: the word is older than computers.
normal.cn: 别只把它和虚拟内存挂钩，这个词比计算机古老得多。

normal.en: A virtual monopoly is one in fact, not by law.
normal.cn: virtual monopoly 指事实上的垄断，而非法律上的。

abstract.en: See a desk appear in an empty room once goggles go on.
abstract.cn: 想戴上眼镜后空房间里浮现出一张桌子。

abstract.en: Hear a class talking in a room that has no walls.
abstract.cn: 听一堂课在没有墙的房间里进行。

abstract.en: Think of an oak already folded inside a small acorn.
abstract.cn: 想橡树早已折叠在一颗小橡子里。

examples.en: The town has become a virtual ghost town since the factory closed.
examples.cn: 工厂关闭后，这座小镇几乎成了鬼城。

examples.en: Students attend virtual labs from home.
examples.cn: 学生们在家参加虚拟实验课。

examples.en: He is the virtual head of the department, though someone else has the title.
examples.cn: 尽管头衔在别人身上，他实际上是这个部门的主事人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「沃求尔」——沃师傅求来的那间屋，看着真，其实是屏幕里的虚拟屋。

root: 拉丁语 virtus（力量；德性）→ 中世纪拉丁语 virtualis（有效力的）→ 英语 virtual

sensesIntro.en: One word about power becomes about effect, then about nearness, then about worlds made of software.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个关于力量的词先变成关于效力，再变成关于接近，最后变成关于由软件造出的世界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a desk appearing in an empty room through goggles.
core.cn: 核心意象：透过眼镜在空房里浮现的桌子。

branches.en: The effect branch: a monopoly in fact, not in law.
branches.cn: 效力分支：事实上的垄断。

branches.en: The nearness branch: almost no evidence at all.
branches.cn: 接近分支：几乎没有证据。

branches.en: The screen branch: a classroom without walls.
branches.cn: 屏幕分支：没有墙的教室。

branches.en: The philosophy branch: the oak inside the acorn.
branches.cn: 哲学分支：橡子里的橡树。

branches.en: The machine branch: memory the computer borrows from disk.
branches.cn: 机器分支：电脑从硬盘借来的内存。

intro.en: The stem virt- means power or worth; -ual makes the adjective and -ly the adverb.
intro.cn: 词干 virt- 意为力量或价值，-ual 构成形容词，-ly 构成副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin virtus gave Medieval Latin virtualis and English virtual, with virtue as a close cousin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 virtus 派生中世纪拉丁语 virtualis 与英语 virtual，virtue 是近亲。

items.example: Virt- carries the idea of a working power.
items.exampleCN: virt- 携带一种起作用的力。

items.example: Virtual means relating to a power in effect.
items.exampleCN: virtual 意为与效力相关的。

items.example: Virtually means in effect.
Virtuality names the quality of being virtual.
Virtuous means full of virtue.
A virtual win is not an actual one.
items.exampleCN: virtual 的胜利不等于 actual 的胜利。

items.example: A virtual ban is an effective ban.
items.exampleCN: 事实上的禁令就是有效的禁令。

items.example: A simulated flight trains pilots.
items.exampleCN: 模拟飞行用来训练飞行员。

items.example: Virtual reality is paired with real reality.
items.exampleCN: virtual reality 与真实现实相对。

definition_en: almost entirely, or in effect, or by means of a computer simulation
core_image: 一间空荡荡的教室，屏幕上却坐满了人
scene: 考试前一周，老师发现班里的座位几乎空了一半，学生都在线上听课。Virtually every student had watched the lecture online before the test.
sceneCN: 这里 virtually 是「几乎、差不多」（第 1 个义项：接近全部但未绝对如此）；句意为考试前几乎每个学生都在网上看过这节课。空了一半的教室正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 去后缀 -ly 构成的形容词，义为「实质上的；虚拟的」
同源名词，义为「美德；优点」
加后缀 -ize 构成，义为「虚拟化」

senses.title: Almost, for practical purposes
senses.definition: almost completely, with only a very small exception
senses.definitionCN: 几乎完全如此，只有极小的例外
senses.example: Virtually every student had watched the lecture online before the test.
senses.exampleCN: 考试前几乎每个学生都在网上看过这节课。
senses.why: From virtue in the old sense of power or effect: what holds in effect holds almost everywhere.
senses.whyCN: 源自古义为「效力」的 virtue：在效力上成立的，就几乎处处成立。

senses.title: In effect, though not in name
senses.definition: in practice or in effect, even if not formally so
senses.definitionCN: 实际上如此，尽管名义上并非如此
senses.example: The two plans are virtually the same.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个计划实际上是一样的。
senses.why: When a difference exists only on paper, the adverb says the effect is the same.
senses.whyCN: 当差别只存在于纸面上时，这个副词就说明效果相同。

senses.title: By computer simulation
senses.definition: by means of a computer model or online environment rather than in person
senses.definitionCN: 通过计算机模型或网络环境而非实体方式
senses.example: The whole factory was tested virtually before it was built.
senses.exampleCN: 整座工厂在建造前先做了虚拟测试。
senses.why: Modern computing gave virtual a new sense, and the adverb followed it into the lab.
senses.whyCN: 现代计算给了 virtual 新义，副词也随它走进了实验室。

senses.title: By remote or online means
senses.definition: through online channels instead of a physical place
senses.definitionCN: 通过线上渠道而非实体场所
senses.example: Half the team works virtually from other cities.
senses.exampleCN: 团队一半的人在其他城市远程工作。
senses.why: A meeting held on screens is held in effect, so the adverb covers remote work.
senses.whyCN: 在屏幕上开的会实际上也是会，副词因此也涵盖远程工作。

senses.title: Nearly, but not quite
senses.definition: close to a state without reaching it fully
senses.definitionCN: 接近某状态但尚未完全达到
senses.example: The old road is virtually gone under the new houses.
senses.exampleCN: 那条老路在新房子下几乎不见了。
senses.why: The word keeps a small door open, since virtually stops short of completely.
senses.whyCN: 这个词始终留着一道小门，因为 virtually 并不等于 completely。

intro.en: Virtually is virtual plus -ly; virtual comes from virtue, once meaning power or effect.
intro.cn: virtually 是 virtual 加 -ly；virtual 来自 virtue，古义为力量、效力。

items.en: Virtus meant worth, courage, and power, from vir, a man.
items.cn: virtus 意为价值、勇气与力量，源自 vir（男子）。

items.en: French vertu kept the sense of power or efficacy.
items.cn: 法语 vertu 保留了「力量、效力」之义。

items.en: English virtue covered moral worth and also active power.
items.cn: 中世纪英语的 virtue 兼指德行与实效力。

items.en: Virtual, and then virtually, meant effective in practice though not in name.
items.cn: virtual 及 virtually 表示名义上不是而实际上有效。

items.en: Computing added the sense of simulated by machine.
items.cn: 计算技术增加了「由机器模拟」之义。

note.en: The first group holds the virtual family, the second the adverbs of nearness and reality.
note.cn: 第一组是 virtual 词族，第二组是表示「近乎」与「实际」的副词。

normalIntro.en: Power in the old sense became effect in practice, and then the world seen on screens.
normalIntro.cn: 古义的力量变成实际效力，再变成屏幕上所见的那个世界。

normal.en: Virtual plus -ly gives the adverb; nothing changes in the stem.
normal.cn: virtual 加 -ly 即副词，词干不变。

normal.en: Virtually every goes together in reports and studies.
normal.cn: 报告与研究里常用 virtually every。

normal.en: Virtually is not exactly: the door to completely stays ajar.
normal.cn: virtually 并不等于 exactly，通往 completely 的门没全关。

normal.en: The word starts with virtue, not with virus.
normal.cn: 这个词开头是 virtue，不是 virus。

normal.en: The stress falls on the first syllable: VIR-tu-al-ly.
normal.cn: 重音在第一音节：VIR-tu-al-ly。

abstract.en: See half-empty seats and lit screens.
abstract.cn: 想一半空着的座位与亮着的屏幕。

abstract.en: Picture a factory tested in a model first.
abstract.cn: 想工厂先在模型里被检验一遍。

abstract.en: Hear a voice on a headset saying it is almost done.
abstract.cn: 听耳机里的声音说差不多完成了。

examples.en: The town was virtually cut off by the snow.
examples.cn: 大雪几乎把这座小镇与外界隔绝。

examples.en: Virtually all the tickets were sold by noon.
examples.cn: 几乎所有票在中午前就卖光了。

examples.en: They met virtually for the first three months.
examples.cn: 头三个月他们都是线上见面。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「蜗牛其实」——蜗牛其实几乎不往前走，看着像没动。

root: 拉丁语 vir（男子）→ virtus（价值、力量）→ 古法语 vertu → virtue → virtual + -ly → virtually

sensesIntro.en: One adverb says almost, says in effect, and says through a screen: three ways of nearly being true.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个副词既说「几乎」，也说「实际上」，还说「隔着屏幕」，都是「近乎成真」的三种方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: empty seats, screens filled with faces.
core.cn: 核心意象：空座位与坐满屏幕的人脸。

branches.en: The almost branch: nearly every student, nearly the same, nearly gone.
branches.cn: 近乎分支：几乎每个学生、几乎一样、几乎消失。

branches.en: The effect branch: two plans alike in practice.
branches.cn: 效力分支：两个计划实际一样。

branches.en: The model branch: a factory tested on a computer.
branches.cn: 模型分支：在计算机里测试的工厂。

branches.en: The remote branch: a team spread across cities.
branches.cn: 远程分支：分散在各地办公的团队。

branches.en: The old road branch: a path lost under houses.
branches.cn: 老路分支：被房屋盖掉的路。

intro.en: The stem virt- means worth or power; -ual makes the adjective and -ly the adverb.
intro.cn: 词干 virt- 意为价值或力量，-ual 构成形容词，-ly 构成副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin virtus, from vir, man, meant worth and power; English virtual turned power into practical effect, and computing turned effect into simulation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 virtus（源自 vir「男子」）意为价值与力量；英语 virtual 把力量转为实际效力，计算技术又把效力转为模拟。

items.example: Virt- holds the sense of power.
Virtual means having the power in effect.
items.exampleCN: virtual 意为在效力上具备。

items.example: Virtually says it holds in effect.
items.exampleCN: virtually 表示在效果上成立。

items.example: Virtualize turns machines into models.
Virtue once meant active power.
Vir is the oldest link in the chain.
items.exampleCN: vir 是这条链上最早的环节。

items.example: Practically and virtually overlap.
items.exampleCN: practically 与 virtually 意义交叠。

items.example: Virtually stops short of completely.
items.exampleCN: virtually 不到 completely 的程度。
